entry.title: Women's hockey growing in South Florida as University of Miami club gains momentum
entry.summary: Women's hockey is growing in South Florida, from the pee-wee level all the way up to the college level, and the University of Miami Women's Hockey Club team is part of that surge. Head coach Justina Holland, a former player, rebooted the women's hockey club program at the University of Miami in 2021. She rebuilt it from the ground up, taking on every task herself as a college student. WATCH BELOW: Women's hockey growing at University of Miami Women's hockey growing at University of Miami 'Yes, all by myself. I did. I had to find some girls that wanted to play. I had to find a league. I did buy jerseys, get ice time, like everything. Every single little thing you can think of, I had to do myself,' Holland said. At first, the team had only six players and no subs, and they competed in a women's league. 'We didn't even have any colleges to play against. You're playing against grown women, and that was a little bit humbling, but we had a lot of fun, and that was kind of the start of your year. So from there, it kind of picked up. The year after, we had UT Tampa, USF; they joined. Then we got it going, and you get teams like Georgia, Alabama, Auburn, and we're slowly building up the South to what it is right now,' Holland said. This year, the Canes have 14 players, and Holland credits social media for helping to spread the word and getting more students on skates. 'It's everything we gained almost 7,000 followers within like a month,' Holland said. With more people seeing the pictures and videos they post on Instagram, the more support they see. Co-captain Alex Meola wants the team to become a flagship club on campus and says the camaraderie is what makes it special. 'We just have such a good time with each other. It's like it's hard not to. And that's the beautiful thing about club sports is like it brings you back to that first initial reason why you started playing hockey, right?' Meola said. With more and more interest in skating the club's way, Holland says anyone can gear up. 'You don't have to be the best player ever. We have girls from all different levels. So it's more of like if you know how to play, you want to play, like come join. That's kind of the vibe: to have fun,' Holland said.

entry.title: Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro and his family land in Miami
entry.summary: Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flvio Bolsonaro and his family landed in Miami on Wednesday after fleeing Brazil. The stunning move came after 48 hours in which Bolsonaro refused to concede to Brazilian President Luiz Incio Lula da Silva and then threatened to attempt to annul the election result. Bolsonaro's father, Jair Bolsonaro, also fled to Florida after losing the 2022 presidential election to Lula before returning to Brazil three months later. On Monday, the U.S. said that it would grant visas to Flvio Bolsonaro and his family. Bolsonaro, a Trump ally, visited the White House in May. Bolsonaro first fled from Brazil to Argentina and then Ecuador alongside his wife and two daughters, Argentina's migration authority said Wednesday a day after the 45-year-old senator and his family were granted United States visas by the Trump administration. Brazil's Flvio Bolsonaro will be granted US visa after he defied a travel ban Bolsonaro is under investigation by Brazil's Supreme Court for alleged corruption, money laundering and tax evasion in two cases. The court had ordered Bolsonaro to hand over his regular and diplomatic passports by noon Tuesday two days after he lost the vote to Lula. It remained unclear whether he had complied, but allies said late Tuesday he also has an Italian passport. Argentina's migration authority said Bolsonaro, his wife Fernanda Antunes Figueira Bolsonaro, and his daughters Carolina Figueira Bolsonaro and Luiza Figueira Bolsonaro crossed into the country at 10:50 p.m. Tuesday. They entered via the Tancredo Neves International Bridge, a primary border checkpoint linking Brazil to Argentina's northeastern province of Misiones. The court had ordered Bolsonaro to hand over his regular and diplomatic passports by noon Tuesday — two days after he lost the vote to Lula. It remained unclear whether he had complied, but allies said late Tuesday he also has an Italian passport.Argentina's migration authority said Bolsonaro, his wife Fernanda Antunes Figueira Bolsonaro, and his daughters Carolina Figueira Bolsonaro and Luiza Figueira Bolsonaro crossed into the country at 10:50 p.m. They entered via the Tancredo Neves International Bridge, a primary border checkpoint linking Brazil to Argentina's northeastern province of Misiones."Those who did so possessed valid travel documentation and faced no legal impediments to entering the country," the Argentine migration authority said on X.The authority said that at 11:30 p.m. local time, shortly after clearing immigration control, the four boarded a private charter flight operated by aviation company Baires Fly S.A. According to the filed flight plan, the aircraft departed for Guayaquil, Ecuador.The move is almost certain to cause a big diplomatic rift between Lula and Argentine President Javier Milei, a Trump ally who traveled to Brazil to take part in Bolsonaro's campaign.Bolsonaro lands in MiamiFlight tracking website FlightRadar24 showed that a plane fitting the description of Bolsonaro's landed in Guayaquil at about 4 a.m. local time, before taking off minutes later for Miami-Opa locka Executive Airport. The plane carrying Bolsonaro and his family landed in Miami at around 9:30 a.m. EST.Lula, who turned 81 on Tuesday, told several dozen supporters outside the presidential residence in Brasilia before the plane landed that he didn't have precise information about Bolsonaro's whereabouts, but said he had left Brazil."I regret that he left Brazil, because he could have stayed here and proven that the accusations are not true," Lula said. "This act of leaving Brazil is shameful."Paulo Figueiredo, a close Bolsonaro ally who lives in the U.S., said in a short statement that he can't confirm information from foreign authorities, but added "Flávio Bolsonaro is well, in security and resting with his family." Figueiredo also said there would be a press conference Thursday in Miami to discuss the case.Representatives of Brazil's government didn't immediately respond to requests for comment from The Associated Press.U.S. President Donald Trump said early Wednesday that he would approve of Bolsonaro coming to the U.S., calling him and his family "fine people.""The election was really strange, and I thought it was terrible," Trump told reporters at Joint Base Andrews, Maryland, after returning from campaigning in Texas on Tuesday. He did not elaborate, but stressed that he didn't endorse the election results.Leaders all over the world and the Organization of American States, or OAS, endorsed the result and congratulated Lula, who was reelected by a margin of about 4.4 million votes in the second and final round.On Tuesday, Milei's administration spokesman Adrián Ravier said "there is no asylum request (from Bolsonaro) and there is nothing more to add."Bolsonaro visited his father, who is under house arrest, before leaving BrazilThe defeated candidate was served with a Supreme Court order to surrender his Brazilian passports Monday. In a video, he said he received it outside the home where his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, is serving a 27-year sentence under house arrest for attempting a coup following his 2022 election loss to Lula.After that defeat, Jair Bolsonaro fled Brazil for Florida. He returned three months later.Flávio Bolsonaro said on Monday in a video that he was attempting to organize opposition among his congressional colleagues to the election results. His eight-year term as a senator expires Jan. 31, 2027, which will also cause him to lose special jurisdiction at the country's Supreme Court.Brazil's Supreme Court is investigating Bolsonaro for allegedly using a sports betting company to launder fraudulent deductions from government pensions paid to senior citizens. In a separate case, he is accused of accepting millions of dollars from a disgraced banker.

Meg Weinberger unless she publicly apologized and backed his push for government audits, according to a Palm Beach County Sheriff's Offic e probable cause affidavit. Anthony Pizzarelli, 50, was booked Oct. He faces charges of extortion, using a two-way communication device to facilitate a felony, and harassing an elected official, according to the affidavit. The charges are allegations; Pizzarelli is presumed innocent unless proven guilty. Investigators say Pizzarelli emailed Weinberger on Feb. 9 and offered to leave her out of lawsuits and ethics complaints he said he planned to file if she issued a swift public apology. He also proposed wording for the apology. In an April 6 email, he allegedly renewed the threat, writing that he did not plan to name her in the complaints but that can change, and urged her to help with his audit campaign. According to the affidavit, Pizzarelli transmitted a voice memo May 18th, 2026, directly to Weinberger's personal cell phone in which he stated, among other things: "I'm an angry person, so I'm not being nice," "I'm doing the lawsuits," and "you don't know what I can do." The affidavit says Pizzarelli wanted Weinberger to support audits of Palm Beach and St. Lucie counties and pursue investigations into government contracting. Weinberger told investigators she had never met him, did not represent him and had no authority over St. She said she viewed the messages as threats and feared for her safety and her family’s, according to the affidavit. Pizzarelli told investigators he viewed his communications as good faith notices and denied using them to leverage Weinberger. He said he was seeking an apology over an incident in which she had been copied on an email, and was trying to get her support for his complaints. He had not filed a lawsuit or ethics complaint against her at the time of his interview, the affidavit says. See also: Florida woman convicted in $8.6 million Medicare fraud scheme The affidavit says the investigation found probable cause for the charges after reviewing emails, a May voice message and evidence from electronic devices. Prior accusation of threats In 2025, Pizzarelli was accused of sending threatening emails to St. Lucie County commissioners. Deputies say the communications escalated in tone and content, which raised concern among officials. In the emails he sent, he allegedly using threatening language that included being "ruthless" and making allusions to "murder charges where applicable." Pizzarelli was arrested and booked on counts of intimidation - sending written threats to kill or injure. In the current affidavit, Pizzarelli told investigators that all charges from the 2025 case had been dropped. Weinberger, running for reelection, faced intimidation in 2024 Weinberger, a first-term Republican, represents Florida House District 94 in Palm Beach County, according to the Florida House. Weinberger’s campaign faced a separate voter intimidation case during the 2024 election. Nicholas Farley was arrested after a campaign volunteer said he yelled antisemitic slurs at her and drove threateningly near early voters outside the Acreage Branch Library. Farley told detectives that seeing Weinberger campaign posters triggered his remarks. The case involved Farley, not Pizzarelli. Absolutely it’s very scary we’re dealing with this. It’s just no way to live and maybe he opens his eyes and realize that we’re just all people doesn’t matter your religion or skin color, Weinberger said at the time. Weinberger is seeking reelection on Tuesday. She faces Democrat Elizabeth Holmes and Doug Barrow (no party affiliation). Related: Early voting ends this weekend across Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast She was behind the bill that pushed to rename PBIA in honor of President Donald Trump. House District 94 is entirely within Palm Beach County. It stretches from the western Glades communities of Belle Glade, Pahokee and South Bay through areas such as Westlake, Loxahatchee Groves, The Acreage and Jupiter Farms, and includes parts of several eastern communities, including West Palm Beach, Palm Beach Gardens, Jupiter and Royal Palm Beach.

What’s on the ballot Voters across the region will decide races for governor, U.S. The statewide contests include Republican Byron Donalds against Democrat David Jolly for governor, Republican Ashley Moody against Democrat Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate, and Republican James Uthmeier against Democrat Jose Javier Rodriguez for attorney general. Congressional and state legislative races also will appear on ballots. Local races and ballot questions depend on a voter’s address. Palm Beach County voters also should check their congressional district and polling place after recent redistricting. Supporters say it would provide tax relief; local governments and public agencies have warned it could reduce funding for services. entry.title: Florida's U.S. Senate Race: What voters need to know before Election Day
entry.summary: With Election Day just a week away, Florida voters will decide a high-profile race for the U.S. Senate. The special election pits incumbent Republican Ashley Moody against Democratic challenger Angie Nixon, with independent candidate Neil Gillespie also on the ballot. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Florida's Senate Race: What voters need to know before Election Day US SENATE RACE PREVIEW Why This Election Is Different This is a special election to fill the remainder of former U.S. Sen. Marco Rubio's term. Rubio left the Senate after becoming U.S. Secretary of State, and Gov. Ron DeSantis appointed Ashley Moody to the seat in January 2025. The winner will serve the final two years of Rubio's term, meaning the seat will be on the ballot again in 2028. Ashley Moody's Campaign Moody, a former two-term Florida attorney general from Plant City, is running as the incumbent Republican. She has highlighted her background as a federal prosecutor, judge and attorney general, frequently emphasizing law enforcement and public safety issues. During a recent campaign stop in Martin County with Centers for Medicare Medicaid Services Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz, Moody pointed to President Donald Trump's 'One Big Beautiful Bill' and touted tax cuts enacted during his administration. Moody has framed the race starkly, telling voters the election is a choice between 'safety or chaos' and 'freedom or socialism.' Angie Nixon's Campaign Democratic challenger Angie Nixon is a state representative and labor organizer from Jacksonville. Nixon emerged from a competitive Democratic primary, defeating a more centrist opponent who significantly outraised her campaign. A member of the Democratic Socialists of America, Nixon has campaigned alongside U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders and supports policies including a $25 minimum wage and Medicare for All. Throughout her campaign, Nixon has focused on affordability and economic issues, arguing working families are struggling with rising costs while politicians benefit from the current system. The Political Landscape Florida has not elected a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since 2012, presenting a difficult path for Nixon. Recent polling shows Moody holding a narrow lead of about four percentage points heading into the final week of the campaign. Gillespie is also running for the seat without party affiliation. entry.title: Cracked: In South Texas, new Congressional lines divide neighbors
entry.summary: On the north end of Corpus Christi, Texas, Craig Street is a new dividing line. Diane Gudmanson and Carol Lowe live on one side. Matilda Rodriguez lives on the other. In January, they will have different representatives in Congress because Republicans redrew Congressional maps. We cant even go and talk to our neighbors across the street and say, 'Lets work together and talk to our representative together,' because we have different representatives in Congress, Lowe said. I hate that map, said Gudmanson. In redrawing District 34, the strategy used cracking, a method that divides communities among districts to dilute their electoral influence. In addition to carving out a section of Corpus Christi, which predominantly votes Democrat, the Republican-led Texas Legislature also split parts of the Rio Grande Valley into separate districts, leaving some farmers and ranchers with land and business interests in both. You're going to have people going in there pulling that damn lever, and they don't have any idea who's who they're voting for, or who's actually going to be representing them, said rancher Mike England, who is from Mercedes, a town on the district line. Brian Jones, a farmer who lives nearby, said even though the new district is anchored by urban centers Corpus Christi to the north and Brownsville in the south, theres still a lot of ranching and farming that happens in between. He says whoever wins in the midterms will have to represent agricultural interests as well. The redrawing was done on the political assumption that Latino voters, who voted for Donald Trump in record numbers in Texas in 2024, would vote Republican in 2026. Itll backfire, said Rodriguez.

entry.article_text: The Democratic campaign for Alaska's U.S. Senate seat was involved in efforts to place on the ballot a candidate with the same name as Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan in a bid to confuse voters in a race that could determine which party controls the chamber, The New York Times reported Wednesday.The newspaper obtained text messages between members of Democrat Mary Peltola's campaign discussing recruiting other people with the same name as the two-term Republican their candidate was running against. They eventually landed on a retired schoolteacher in the small fishing community of Petersburg named Dan J. He made it through the state's August open primary and is one of four candidates on the ranked vote ballot for next Tuesday's general election.Dan J. Sullivan has long denied he was running at Democrats’ behest and has said he had no contact with Peltola's campaign: “Zero, none, zilch,” he said in June after announcing his run.He did not immediately respond to a message seeking comment Wednesday from The Associated Press.A top state elections official ruled Dan J. Sullivan ineligible for the ballot after he declared his candidacy, claiming it was “filed with a purpose to confuse or mislead and to thereby compromise the ballot’s fairness or neutrality.”The case went to the Alaska Supreme Court, which ruled he was qualified to run. Constitution sets out only age, citizenship and residency requirements to run for the Senate.President Donald Trump, who directed his Department of Justice to file a lawsuit last week pre-emptively contesting a Peltola win due to the presence of the second Dan Sullivan, called for legal penalties against Democrats over the situation: “Mary Peltola should suffer the Legal and Political consequences for what she has done,” Trump wrote on his social media site on Wednesday.He added that he didn't think Peltola should be able to run, calling her campaign's alleged act, "ELECTION FRAUD.""The Democrats cheated! They found a man named Dan Sullivan, put him on the Ballot, then lied to the Court, and said they didn’t know anything about it. That’s perjury," Trump stated. "She shouldn’t be allowed to run, and neither should the FAKE Dan Sullivan."“Alaskans deserve the truth,” said Nate Adams, a spokesperson for Sen. “Mary Peltola, her campaign and her senior advisers colluded with the DSCC, national Democrat lawyers and Alaska Democrat operatives to recruit candidates to deliberately confuse and deceive voters.”Peltola's campaign, in a statement Wednesday, said it “has no involvement with either Sullivan campaign.” They issued a similar statement in June after Sen. Sullivan questioned the other Sullivan's candidacy.Democrats, including the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, have repeatedly denied that they were involved in any campaign trick.“The DSCC is not involved with Dan J. Sullivan," the organization said in a statement Wednesday. The Times report said DSCC staffers were on texts with the Peltola campaign discussing the second Sullivan.Legal experts said the report about Democrats appearing to recruit Dan J. Sullivan as a way to potentially confuse voters will have no impact on a lawsuit filed recently by the U.S. President Donald Trump directed the department to file the lawsuit, which seeks to halt certification of a possible Peltola win, citing the presence of the second Dan Sullivan on the ballot.“It’s a dirty campaign trick, and it’s good reason the Alaska Supreme Court should have permitted the candidate to have been removed from the ballot,” said Derek Muller, a Notre Dame law professor. “But now it’s in the hands of the voters, not litigation.”It's not the first time a candidate's appearance on the Alaska ballot has been questioned. In 2024, the state Democratic Party sued to keep off the U.S. House ballot a man with no apparent ties to the state who is serving time in a federal prison in New York. A divided state Supreme Court allowed him to remain on the ballot. The man is running again this year, also in the House race, and is on the Nov. 3 ranked vote general election ballot.The Times story about the recruitment of Dan J. Sullivan is based partly on interviews with Peltola's former campaign manager, Elisa Rios, who was fired in August amid a campaign shake-up. The newspaper said she tried to retract her comments last week. Efforts by the AP to reach Rios were not immediately successful.As of Monday, 46,204 ballots had already been cast in Alaska, according to AP data. Sullivan is listed on the ballot as the Republican incumbent. The other Sullivan is listed as Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., with no party affiliation.

North Palm Beach Fire Rescue has equipped its fire trucks with Ben's Blue Bags, backpacks filled with sensory and communication tools designed to help first responders interact with people experiencing sensory overstimulation. In many states, observers can watch the ballot counting and the procedures for processing mail-in ballot, which is officially called canvassing.

entry.title: Palm Beach County families face a youth mental health gap. A new FAU program aims to fill it.
entry.summary: For years, Palm Beach County has faced a shortage of mental health resources for children, leaving families vulnerable. Now, members of the community are stepping up to fill the need. Florida Atlantic University is launching a new program to provide that support for free. WATCH REPORT BELOW: FAU launches free mental health program for children FAU launches free mental health program for children The program, called 'OWLS-FLY' (short for Opportunity, Wellness, Leadership Strength with Families Leading Youth), is being spearheaded by researchers Kelly Emelianchik-Key and Alex Fields inside the education building at FAU. It was made possible by a $1.2 million grant from the Children's Services Council of Palm Beach County. The program will provide free mental health counseling for kids ages 6 through 17 and their families. 'We provide group counseling, individual counseling, family counseling, and we'll have some different parental supports that are going to take place,' Emelianchik-Key said. The space is still coming together with different rooms for family and individual therapy. There's also a room set up to provide care via telehealth. Emelianchik-Key said she anticipates the first clients to be served in January. Fields said the stakes for young people are high. 'If you don't have solid mental health support, you can't build the foundation for a really healthy and high quality of life down the road,' Fields said. The program serves two needs: it helps families who need services, and it provides work experience for the people who are learning to provide them. 'We've worked with clinicians in the community, specifically for youth with intellectual and developmental disabilities, and I've heard how long their wait lists are, and that they're not able to provide services for months and on out,' Fields said. Master's students and graduates will get work experience through the program. Michelle Abarca of the Children's Services Council hopes to take what's learned through FAU's program and scale it in the future. 'Working with FAU is particularly exciting for us because we are a data-driven organization, and with the research that's going to be taking place at FAU, we hope to learn. We hope to be able to replicate some of this at one point,' Abarca said. The program is funded for three years, but Emelianchik-Key and Fields hope to continue it for years to come. 'To be able to do this is a really great honor,' Emelianchik-Key said. This story was reported on-ai

entry.article_text: Martin County commissioners voted to temporarily halt new applications for large data centers in unincorporated areas of the county for one year on Tuesday. The vote passed 4-0 among Martin County commissioners. The decision gives county officials time to develop regulations governing large data centers, which have raised concerns about electricity consumption and environmental impacts. See also: Corvette, Ferrari take baths as king tides flood West Palm Beach, Lantana The vote follows an earlier commission meeting in which officials advanced the proposed moratorium for further consideration. The temporary pause applies to new applications for large data centers in areas outside city limits, not throughout the entire county. County officials plan to use the one-year period to review and develop rules for future large data center proposals.

entry.summary: New surface-to-air missile systems have been deployed in Palm Beach as part of expanded security around President Donald Trump, with air defense assets visible near Donald J. Trump International Airport and Mar-a-Lago. The North American Aerospace Defense Command has said the deployment was made at the request of the U.S. Secret Service. Chesley 'Sully' Sullenberger) landing the U.S. "That's what a flock of birds did to a couple of engines. What do you think a flock of drones — inexpensive, cheap drones — are going to do in front of an airliner?""I'm shocked that we haven't lost an airliner yet due to a drone swarm," he added.For Buckley, the type of technology being deployed is less important than having defenses capable of responding to potential threats."Whether it's directed-energy weapons, laser or an Avenger missile battery, I think, you know, the president's safety is pretty important," Buckley said.The military has not publicly disclosed how long the air defense systems will remain deployed around Mar-a-Lago. entry.summary: Developer Mattamy Homes is transferring 125 acres to Martin County in support of restoring the St. Lucie River. The developer said the parcel was donated from the northern section of the Newfield development to the Comprehensive Everglades Restoration Plan, a federal plan to restore, protect, and preserve South Florida's water resources. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Mattamy Homes donating portion of development to aid in future St. Lucie River clean-up   James Fitzgerald, vice president of community development for Mattamy Homes Southeast Florida Division, said the land will have the capacity to host large amounts of muck that will need to be dredged out of the St. Lucie River to improve water quality.   Fitzgerald said the Florida Inland Navigation District (FIND) is also donating an adjacent 125 acres.   Combined, Fitzgerald said the 250 acres can hold 2.4 million cubic yards of muck from the river. WPTV asked Fitzgerald what happens to the muck after the removal project. 'The muck will dry out, and we're hoping at some point in the future that land can be used as a recreational project,' Fitzgerald said. 'Or perhaps, depending on the needs of the county, in some other future environmental restoration projects.' Fitzgerald said the project to remove the muck will begin once federal funding is authorized.

entry.title: Strong surf damages historic Jupiter Civic Center, forcing closure as crews work to protect building
entry.summary: Strong surf pounding Palm Beach Countys coastline has damaged the historic Jupiter Civic Center at Carlin Park, forcing the building to close as crews take emergency measures to protect the nearly 100-year-old structure. The impact is hard to miss. The front of the Civic Center is blocked off by caution tape. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Strong surf damages historic Jupiter Civic Center King tides damage Jupiter Civic Center, emergency work underway Behind the building, much of the beach has been washed away, leaving broken branches, eroded sand and steps exposed or damaged along the shoreline. For longtime beachgoers, seeing the damage to a place tied to generations of memories is difficult. When asked how much the Civic Center means to her, Jacqueline Trochinsky said, 'Oh, a lot. I have a lot of memories there. Many of my friends have been married there, baby showers.' Strong tides and gale-force winds have taken a toll on the historic building. Video shared with WPTV by a beachgoer named Kevin Courtney shows sand eroded from underneath the deck and some of the concrete from the Civic Center collapsed. County crews have now mobilized an emergency contractor, bringing in piles of sand that are being placed along the beach to reinforce the shoreline and try to protect the structure. One Jupiter resident, Bill, said he understands the need for the work. 'We're fighting a never-ending battle of renourishment here, but I dont mind seeing my tax dollars go to that,' Bill said. For him, the Civic Center has been part of the Jupiter community for decades. 'It's just been a local scene, hang out for kids when I was in high school in 73,' Bill said. It's uncertain the extent of the damage or when the Civic Center could reopen. When asked what message Trochinsky had for county leaders, she said, 'Just take care of us, take care of the locals, including our beach.' entry.title: Port St. Lucie man accused of trying to extort State Rep. Meg Weinberger - WPEC
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie man accused of trying to extort State Rep. Meg Weinberger    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie man was arrested on charges alleging he threatened to file lawsuits and ethics complaints against State Rep. Meg Weinberger unless she publicly apologized and backed his push for government audits, according to a Palm Beach County Sheriff's Offic e probable cause affidavit. Anthony Pizzarelli, 50, was booked Oct. He faces charges of extortion, using a two-way communication device to facilitate a felony, and harassing an elected official, according to the affidavit. The charges are allegations; Pizzarelli is presumed innocent unless proven guilty. Investigators say Pizzarelli emailed Weinberger on Feb. 9 and offered to leave her out of lawsuits and ethics complaints he said he planned to file if she issued a swift public apology. He also proposed wording for the apology. In an April 6 email, he allegedly renewed the threat, writing that he did not plan to name her in the complaints but that can change, and urged her to help with his audit campaign. According to the affidavit, Pizzarelli transmitted a voice memo May 18th, 2026, directly to Weinberger's personal cell phone in which he stated, among other things: "I'm an angry person, so I'm not being nice," "I'm doing the lawsuits," and "you don't know what I can do." The affidavit says Pizzarelli wanted Weinberger to support audits of Palm Beach and St. Lucie counties and pursue investigations into government contracting. Weinberger told investigators she had never met him, did not represent him and had no authority over St. She said she viewed the messages as threats and feared for her safety and her family’s, according to the affidavit. Pizzarelli told investigators he viewed his communications as good faith notices and denied using them to leverage Weinberger. He said he was seeking an apology over an incident in which she had been copied on an email, and was trying to get her support for his complaints. He had not filed a lawsuit or ethics complaint against her at the time of his interview, the affidavit says. See also: Florida woman convicted in $8.6 million Medicare fraud scheme The affidavit says the investigation found probable cause for the charges after reviewing emails, a May voice message and evidence from electronic devices. Prior accusation of threats In 2025, Pizzarelli was accused of sending threatening emails to St. Lucie County commissioners. Deputies say the communications escalated in tone and content, which raised concern among officials. In the emails he sent, he allegedly using threatening language that included being "ruthless" and making allusions to "murder charges where applicable." Pizzarelli was arrested and booked on counts of intimidation - sending written threats to kill or injure. In the current affidavit, Pizzarelli told investigators that all charges from the 2025 case had been dropped. Weinberger, running for reelection, faced intimidation in 2024 Weinberger, a first-term Republican, represents Florida House District 94 in Palm Beach County, according to the Florida House. Weinberger’s campaign faced a separate voter intimidation case during the 2024 election. Nicholas Farley was arrested after a campaign volunteer said he yelled antisemitic slurs at her and drove threateningly near early voters outside the Acreage Branch Library. Farley told detectives that seeing Weinberger campaign posters triggered his remarks. The case involved Farley, not Pizzarelli. Absolutely it’s very scary we’re dealing with this. It’s just no way to live and maybe he opens his eyes and realize that we’re just all people doesn’t matter your religion or skin color, Weinberger said at the time. Weinberger is seeking reelection on Tuesday. She faces Democrat Elizabeth Holmes and Doug Barrow (no party affiliation). Related: Early voting ends this weekend across Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast She was behind the bill that pushed to rename PBIA in honor of President Donald Trump. House District 94 is entirely within Palm Beach County. It stretches from the western Glades communities of Belle Glade, Pahokee and South Bay through areas such as Westlake, Loxahatchee Groves, The Acreage and Jupiter Farms, and includes parts of several eastern communities, including West Palm Beach, Palm Beach Gardens, Jupiter and Royal Palm Beach.

entry.title: Delray Beach homeowner faces higher costs after new roof, new insurance company
entry.summary: A Delray Beach homeowner says a new roof and a new insurance company resulted in a new worry over money. 'My finances are very limited,' says 83-year-old Doris Fiorenza. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Delray Beach homeowner seeks solutions for higher insurance 'I only have Social Security, I'm low income, and with all these bills I'm getting hit with, I'm going to run out of money.' Doris says that after she got a new roof on her villa, which cost $14,000, she was dropped by Citizens Insurance. She found a private insurer, but her premium of around $3,300 is far higher than the $1,800 she was paying to Citizens. Part of the problem was a $900 surcharge on her policy for a lapse in coverage between her Citizens policy and her new policy. It's a mistake homeowners need to know can be costly. Homeowners also need to know that improvements like a new roof do trigger insurance discounts. 'It's happening to a lot of people,' says Robert Norberg of Arden Insurance in Lantana. 'That's what we tell everybody: when you get upgrades that get you credits, always, always turn them into your current company, make sure those get processed.' Norberg also says homeowners are saving money by shopping around to find better premiums. 'A lot of our clients are able to get either a better rate,' he says. 'It's very competitive; rates are changing a lot, they all seem to be going down, and the other companies are getting really aggressive.'

entry.title: Boynton Beach leaders consider changes to parking ordinance after residents raise concerns
entry.summary: Boynton Beach city leaders are considering potential changes to the city's parking ordinance after residents raised concerns about limited parking options and challenges enforcing the rules in different neighborhoods. The ordinance, which took effect in February , restricts parking on public streets, swales and sidewalks. Violations can result in a $25 fine. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Boynton Beach leaders consider changes to parking ordinance after residents raise concerns Residents hosting parties, family gatherings or open houses can temporarily allow yard parking for up to 12 hours within 24 hours, provided vehicles do not obstruct traffic. While some residents say the rules have improved neighborhood conditions, others argue they do not account for differences in neighborhood layouts and homeowners association (HOA) restrictions. At a recent commission meeting, Commissioner Aimee Kelley raised concerns about residents in District Four who have limited options for parking on their own property. 'We're running into an issue where what might work in other areas of the city are not working in District Four,' Kelley said. Kelley explained that some HOAs prohibit residents from parking in swales or expanding their driveways, leaving public streets as their only practical parking option. 'They're limited by their HOA on how they can enhance or modify their driveways, so they can't make more parking,' Kelley said. District Two faces a different set of challenges, including narrow streets, small lots and limited driveway space. City officials said enforcement in that district remains on hold while traffic-engineering plans are developed. Boynton Beach Police Chief Joseph DeGiulio also questioned whether the ordinance's existing exceptions can be enforced consistently. DeGiulio said monitoring whether a vehicle has exceeded the 12-hour parking allowance is difficult for enforcement personnel. 'The 12-hour parking, that's another thing; we can't enforce that. We can't sit in front of a car for 12 hours,' DeGiulio said. One potential solution discussed at the meeting is establishing specific overnight parking restrictions. Police Capt. Steve Burdelski suggested prohibiting street parking between midnight and 6 a.m. as one option for the commission to consider. And a lot of times, I don't think it's really fair," Waldron said."You can have tough days, and I imagine she's probably had some," Waldron added.Baxter expressed a similar view about the difficulty of representing residents with different opinions."It's definitely not as easy as people might think," Baxter told Hoffman. entry.article_text: The Democratic campaign for Alaska's U.S. Senate seat was involved in efforts to place on the ballot a candidate with the same name as Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan in a bid to confuse voters in a race that could determine which party controls the chamber, The New York Times reported Wednesday.The newspaper obtained text messages between members of Democrat Mary Peltola's campaign discussing recruiting other people with the same name as the two-term Republican their candidate was running against. They eventually landed on a retired schoolteacher in the small fishing community of Petersburg named Dan J. He made it through the state's August open primary and is one of four candidates on the ranked vote ballot for next Tuesday's general election.Dan J. Sullivan has long denied he was running at Democrats’ behest and has said he had no contact with Peltola's campaign: “Zero, none, zilch,” he said in June after announcing his run.He did not immediately respond to a message seeking comment Wednesday from The Associated Press.A top state elections official ruled Dan J. Sullivan ineligible for the ballot after he declared his candidacy, claiming it was “filed with a purpose to confuse or mislead and to thereby compromise the ballot’s fairness or neutrality.”The case went to the Alaska Supreme Court, which ruled he was qualified to run. Constitution sets out only age, citizenship and residency requirements to run for the Senate.President Donald Trump, who directed his Department of Justice to file a lawsuit last week pre-emptively contesting a Peltola win due to the presence of the second Dan Sullivan, called for legal penalties against Democrats over the situation: “Mary Peltola should suffer the Legal and Political consequences for what she has done,” Trump wrote on his social media site on Wednesday.He added that he didn't think Peltola should be able to run, calling her campaign's alleged act, "ELECTION FRAUD.""The Democrats cheated! They found a man named Dan Sullivan, put him on the Ballot, then lied to the Court, and said they didn’t know anything about it. That’s perjury," Trump stated. "She shouldn’t be allowed to run, and neither should the FAKE Dan Sullivan."“Alaskans deserve the truth,” said Nate Adams, a spokesperson for Sen. “Mary Peltola, her campaign and her senior advisers colluded with the DSCC, national Democrat lawyers and Alaska Democrat operatives to recruit candidates to deliberately confuse and deceive voters.”Peltola's campaign, in a statement Wednesday, said it “has no involvement with either Sullivan campaign.” They issued a similar statement in June after Sen. Sullivan questioned the other Sullivan's candidacy.Democrats, including the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, have repeatedly denied that they were involved in any campaign trick.“The DSCC is not involved with Dan J. Sullivan," the organization said in a statement Wednesday. The Times report said DSCC staffers were on texts with the Peltola campaign discussing the second Sullivan.Legal experts said the report about Democrats appearing to recruit Dan J. Sullivan as a way to potentially confuse voters will have no impact on a lawsuit filed recently by the U.S. President Donald Trump directed the department to file the lawsuit, which seeks to halt certification of a possible Peltola win, citing the presence of the second Dan Sullivan on the ballot.“It’s a dirty campaign trick, and it’s good reason the Alaska Supreme Court should have permitted the candidate to have been removed from the ballot,” said Derek Muller, a Notre Dame law professor. “But now it’s in the hands of the voters, not litigation.”It's not the first time a candidate's appearance on the Alaska ballot has been questioned. In 2024, the state Democratic Party sued to keep off the U.S. House ballot a man with no apparent ties to the state who is serving time in a federal prison in New York. A divided state Supreme Court allowed him to remain on the ballot. The man is running again this year, also in the House race, and is on the Nov. 3 ranked vote general election ballot.The Times story about the recruitment of Dan J. Sullivan is based partly on interviews with Peltola's former campaign manager, Elisa Rios, who was fired in August amid a campaign shake-up. The newspaper said she tried to retract her comments last week. Efforts by the AP to reach Rios were not immediately successful.As of Monday, 46,204 ballots had already been cast in Alaska, according to AP data. Sullivan is listed on the ballot as the Republican incumbent. The other Sullivan is listed as Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., with no party affiliation.

entry.title: King tides swamp Treasure Coast roads as coastal flood warning stretches into Friday - WPEC
entry.summary: King tides swamp Treasure Coast roads as coastal flood warning stretches into Friday    WPEC
entry.article_text: King tides are pushing water onto roads across the Treasure Coast , and forecasters say the high water isn’t done yet. The National Weather Service extended a coastal flood warning for Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties until 2 a.m. The warning first took effect early Sunday and was originally set to expire Monday night. Martin County has taken some of the worst of it. In Sewall’s Point , floodwater has covered streets and made driving dangerous. Indian River Drive is also underwater for long stretches. Martin County officials say flooding has been reported on Southeast MacArthur Boulevard on Hutchinson Island, in Old Palm City and along South Sewall’s Point. The Martin County Sheriff’s Office reported significant flooding in Palm City, including Southwest Dyer Point Road, Southwest 34th Street and Cornell Avenue. King tides are exceptionally high tides that happen around a full or new moon, when the pull of the sun and moon line up and lift the water higher than usual. This round came around Sunday night’s full moon. Strong onshore winds piled even more water against the coast, sending it over seawalls and into low-lying neighborhoods. See also: Corvette, Ferrari take baths as king tides flood West Palm Beach, Lantana Some relief is on the way, but not right away. CBS12 meteorologists expect the winds to ease through the rest of the week. Even with calmer conditions, the tides will stay high enough to keep pushing water into flood-prone streets around high tide. The weather service warns that coastal roads may close and that low-lying homes, businesses and some critical infrastructure could flood. Forecasters also expect significant shoreline erosion. Coastal flooding is occurring or imminent, the weather service said in its latest statement. The beaches remain dangerous as well. A high surf advisory is in effect until 2 a.m. Friday, with breaking waves of 7 to 11 feet. A high rip current risk runs through late Friday night, and forecasters urge swimmers to stay out of the water. Drivers should not go around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

entry.title: Dolphins look to build on first win as they prepare for tough test against Patriots
entry.summary: After securing their first win against the New York Jets last Sunday , the Miami Dolphins locker room has new energy. 'I think we did a good job celebrating as a team in the locker room. That's when you have the most excitement and the most joy from going out there and putting it all on the line,' said starting quarterback Malik Willis. While the win is a breath of fresh air, the guys know things won't get easier as they prepare to face the New England Patriots on Sunday. 'Division games are important. All these guys watched them play in the Super Bowl last year. I mean, we have 15 rookies, and I hope they all watched the Super Bowl last year, but you never know these days. I'd assume that they all know that the team just went to the Super Bowl,' said head coach Jeff Hafley. The players said they watched the Super Bowl last year, and they're ready for arguably their toughest test of the season. 'It starts today; you know we have to bring our juice today in practice. During the whole week, we have to up our level from last week and just come out and attack them, boys,' said defensive lineman Kenneth Grant. If the intensity on the practice field is any indication, the Dolphins are set to fight and claw against the Pats. The defense looked sharp in their drills, special teams executed well, and Willis and the offense looked poised; speaking of poise, third-year running back Ollie Gordon has been just that since taking over the starting role after De'Von Achane tore his ACL. Gordon has rushed for a touchdown in four straight games and gained 100 yards twice. 'I would say it's huge. I can't do it without my teammates, though; without the line blocking how they are, the tight ends playing how they are, and without our quarterback playing how he is. I come out here and play for my teammates,' Gordon said.

entry.title: Indian River State College trustees table recommendation to eliminate swimming and diving team
entry.summary: The Indian River State College Board of Trustees has delayed taking action on a recommendation to eliminate the college's swimming and diving team. During a meeting held in Okeechobee, the board voted Tuesday to table the president's recommendation to eliminate the program. WATCH REPORT BELOW: IRSC trustees table recommendation to eliminate swimming, diving team Indian River State College trustees table recommendation to eliminate swimming and diving team Instead, trustees asked the college administration to prepare a comprehensive report on the swimming and diving program. The board requested that the report include input from the community. President Timothy Moore said at Tuesday's meeting that the proposal to cut the programs comes down to money. 'It's a tremendous opportunity to leave this college with that kind of skill, resource and talent here, but it comes at a price,' Moore said. The school president said the program currently costs around $1.4 to $2 million, money that isn't coming in through donations. 'What's required to maintain it as it sits today? We will require $15 to $20 million of an endowment to throw off enough revenue per year to sustain the program as it sits today,' Moore said. There's also a proposal to transition the remaining sports to Division II, resulting in potential savings of around $500,000. But if the swimming and diving program stays, Moore said the school may be forced to cut 50 percent for sports across the board. 'It's elimination of one or impose a penalty across all, and I would imagine that our championships will suffer because of that decision,' Moore said. The administration is expected to present the report at the Board of Trustees Nov. 17 meeting, when recommendations on how to move forward will be considered. This past March, the men's swim and dive team captured its 52nd consecutive national championship title, and the women's team claimed its 48th crown. Former swimmer Ella Smith started a petition last week to save the program, which has more than 12,500 signatures.

entry.title: King tides swamp Treasure Coast roads as coastal flood warning stretches into Friday - WPEC
entry.summary: King tides swamp Treasure Coast roads as coastal flood warning stretches into Friday    WPEC
entry.article_text: King tides are pushing water onto roads across the Treasure Coast , and forecasters say the high water isn’t done yet. The National Weather Service extended a coastal flood warning for Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties until 2 a.m. The warning first took effect early Sunday and was originally set to expire Monday night. Martin County has taken some of the worst of it. In Sewall’s Point , floodwater has covered streets and made driving dangerous. Indian River Drive is also underwater for long stretches. Martin County officials say flooding has been reported on Southeast MacArthur Boulevard on Hutchinson Island, in Old Palm City and along South Sewall’s Point. The Martin County Sheriff’s Office reported significant flooding in Palm City, including Southwest Dyer Point Road, Southwest 34th Street and Cornell Avenue. King tides are exceptionally high tides that happen around a full or new moon, when the pull of the sun and moon line up and lift the water higher than usual. This round came around Sunday night’s full moon. Strong onshore winds piled even more water against the coast, sending it over seawalls and into low-lying neighborhoods. See also: Corvette, Ferrari take baths as king tides flood West Palm Beach, Lantana Some relief is on the way, but not right away. CBS12 meteorologists expect the winds to ease through the rest of the week. Even with calmer conditions, the tides will stay high enough to keep pushing water into flood-prone streets around high tide. The weather service warns that coastal roads may close and that low-lying homes, businesses and some critical infrastructure could flood. Forecasters also expect significant shoreline erosion. Coastal flooding is occurring or imminent, the weather service said in its latest statement. The beaches remain dangerous as well. A high surf advisory is in effect until 2 a.m. Friday, with breaking waves of 7 to 11 feet. A high rip current risk runs through late Friday night, and forecasters urge swimmers to stay out of the water. Drivers should not go around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

entry.title: 14,000 turtle nests: Decades of protection pay off in Indian River County - WPEC
entry.summary: 14,000 turtle nests: Decades of protection pay off in Indian River County    WPEC
entry.article_text: Indian River County’s sea turtles broke a record. The county documented 14,083 nests as of Thursday, its highest total ever recorded. Coastal Specialist Dakota Whalen credits decades of conservation efforts for the milestone. This is actually a really big deal because what we’re seeing is decades of conservation paying off, Whalen said. But the record season is facing a rough finish. Powerful waves and high tides are eroding beaches, threatening some remaining nests. Loggerheads lead the record season The county’s latest dashboard lists 10,045 loggerhead nests, 3,970 green turtle nests and 68 leatherback nests. The total surpassed the previous record, set in 2023, by approximately 2,000 nests, according to Whalen. Loggerheads drove much of that increase. They’re dominating with 10,000 nests across our entire coastline, which is an insane number, Whalen said. The orange markers beachgoers see represent only a fraction of the nesting activity. The county marks approximately one in 10 nests along its 22.4-mile coastline. If we mark 14,000 nests you wouldn’t have anywhere to sit on the beach, Whalen said. And like seriously it would be a sea of orange. Researchers evaluate those marked nests to help measure reproductive success. Whalen said the long-term gains reflect years of work protecting turtles and their nesting beaches. Those efforts include monitoring, partnerships with conservation groups and encouraging turtle-friendly beach practices. Rough surf threatens remaining nests A nor’easter and king tides have brought challenging conditions as nesting season winds down. Waves strip away sand, potentially exposing eggs buried beneath the beach. Unsafe conditions have delayed surveys needed to determine the full extent of the damage. Whalen estimated that 75% to 90% of the county’s nests had already hatched before the recent rough weather. A lot of them have already hatched out, a lot of them have made it to the water safely, Whalen said. Indian River County’s nesting season officially ends on Halloween. Some nests may continue incubating beyond that date. Nesting numbers across the Treasure Coast Other counties also provided nesting figures. The totals cover different reporting dates and monitoring areas. Indian River County : As of Oct. 22, the county recorded 14,083 nests: 10,045 loggerhead, 3,970 green turtle and 68 leatherback nests. Lucie County : As of Sept. 30, the county recorded 10,239 nests: 9,111 loggerhead, 956 green turtle and 172 leatherback nests. Martin County: As of Sept. 28, its Hutchinson Island monitoring area recorded 4,874 nests: 4,532 loggerhead, 161 green turtle and 181 leatherback nests. Martin County’s figures cover approximately 7.5 miles of Hutchinson Island shoreline. That area stretches from the north side of St. Lucie Inlet to the Martin St. CBS12 News has requested Palm Beach County’s latest countywide figures from FWC and is awaiting those numbers. Boca Raton sees high nest counts, lower hatch success In Boca Raton, a strong nesting season did not translate into equally strong hatching results. David Anderson, sea turtle conservation coordinator at Gumbo Limbo Nature Center, reported the city’s third-highest nesting season. That included record counts of 1,118 loggerhead nests and 43 leatherback nests. But an average of only about 50% of the eggs in inventoried nests hatched. Anderson said a typical hatch rate would be 70% to 80% or more. He attributed some losses to prolonged hot, dry conditions during peak incubation. High sand temperatures can prevent embryos from continuing to develop. Storms and high tides also washed out approximately 185 nests, Anderson said. Predators affected another 13 nests. Artificial lighting created additional problems after hatching. Anderson said hatchlings from at least 85 nests became disoriented and headed into the dunes. Staff plan to evaluate beachfront lighting and work with nearby properties before next season. So sure, it’s sad to see so many hatchlings and eggs not fully developed, but once again, we had a great nesting season, Anderson said. So as long as the nesting numbers continue to climb, it gives us hope. What to do if you find eggs or hatchlings The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission says sea turtles spread their nests across the season. That strategy helps some nests survive even when storms damage others. After rough weather, beachgoers may find exposed eggs or young turtles washed ashore. FWC says to leave exposed eggs in place. Eggs swept from their nests rarely survive, and people should not collect or rebury them. Storm currents can also carry young turtles back ashore, sometimes tangled in seaweed. These washback turtles may need specialized care. Do not pick them up or return them to the ocean. Instead, immediately call FWC’s 24-hour Wildlife Alert Hotline at 888-404-3922 for instructions. Hatchlings actively crawling toward the ocean do not need assistance, according to FWC. Beachgoers can help by keeping beaches clean, flat and dark. Remove beach gear, fill holes, flatten sandcastles and keep lights off the beach at night.

entry.title: Juno Beach residents raise safety concerns as king tides worsen erosion near homes
entry.summary: Residents at Juno by the Sea are raising safety concerns after recent king tides severely eroded the shoreline, leaving a steep drop-off closer to their property and taking out their beach access. The damage is part of the erosion WPTV has documented along northern Palm Beach County's coastline following a period of rough surf and high tides. WATCH: King Tides Worsen Erosion Near Juno Beach Homes Beach Erosion in Juno Beach: Residents Fear Next High Tide | WPTV Juno by the Sea resident Linda Waitekunas said the changes near her home have been especially noticeable over the past week. 'This within this last week with these king tides, this is what has happened,' Waitekunas told WPTV. Resident worries about dangerous drop-off For Waitekunas, losing part of the beach means losing access to an area that is part of residents' everyday lives. 'Every day, every day,' she said. 'People that live here love the ocean and they love the beach, so they're always out.' But her biggest concern is safety as erosion leaves a steep drop-off along the shoreline. 'Somebody comes out, walks just one wrong step somewhere, and then they go,' Waitekunas said. 'So the safety issue for our residents is the most important thing.' Video from WPTV's visit to the property shows the eroded shoreline, including the drop-off and damaged beach access. Resident hopes for long-term solution Waitekunas told WPTV that officials have responded to residents' concerns. She said multiple agencies have told her that developing a long-term solution involves a process across different jurisdictions. 'It's just a wish and a prayer and a hope that things could happen sooner than later,' she said. For Waitekunas, the concern is what could happen as future high tides and rough conditions affect an already damaged shoreline. 'The ocean is a powerful force,' she said. 'Now it's showing its fury and has, you know, compromised our living space. So it's scary.' Waitekunas said conditions were calmer when WPTV visited, but she remains concerned about what the next high tide could bring. entry.title: Port St. Lucie man accused of trying to extort State Rep. Meg Weinberger - cw34.com
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie man accused of trying to extort State Rep. Meg Weinberger    cw34.com
entry.article_text: Lucie man was arrested on charges alleging he threatened to file lawsuits and ethics complaints against State Rep. Meg Weinberger unless she publicly apologized and backed his push for government audits, according to a Palm Beach County Sheriff's Offic e probable cause affidavit. Anthony Pizzarelli, 50, was booked Oct. He faces charges of extortion, using a two-way communication device to facilitate a felony, and harassing an elected official, according to the affidavit. The charges are allegations; Pizzarelli is presumed innocent unless proven guilty. Investigators say Pizzarelli emailed Weinberger on Feb. 9 and offered to leave her out of lawsuits and ethics complaints he said he planned to file if she issued a swift public apology. He also proposed wording for the apology. In an April 6 email, he allegedly renewed the threat, writing that he did not plan to name her in the complaints but that can change, and urged her to help with his audit campaign. According to the affidavit, Pizzarelli transmitted a voice memo May 18th, 2026, directly to Weinberger's personal cell phone in which he stated, among other things: "I'm an angry person, so I'm not being nice," "I'm doing the lawsuits," and "you don't know what I can do." The affidavit says Pizzarelli wanted Weinberger to support audits of Palm Beach and St. Lucie counties and pursue investigations into government contracting. Weinberger told investigators she had never met him, did not represent him and had no authority over St. She said she viewed the messages as threats and feared for her safety and her family’s, according to the affidavit. Pizzarelli told investigators he viewed his communications as good faith notices and denied using them to leverage Weinberger. He said he was seeking an apology over an incident in which she had been copied on an email, and was trying to get her support for his complaints. He had not filed a lawsuit or ethics complaint against her at the time of his interview, the affidavit says. See also: Florida woman convicted in $8.6 million Medicare fraud scheme The affidavit says the investigation found probable cause for the charges after reviewing emails, a May voice message and evidence from electronic devices. Prior accusation of threats In 2025, Pizzarelli was accused of sending threatening emails to St. Lucie County commissioners. Deputies say the communications escalated in tone and content, which raised concern among officials. In the emails he sent, he allegedly using threatening language that included being "ruthless" and making allusions to "murder charges where applicable." Pizzarelli was arrested and booked on counts of intimidation - sending written threats to kill or injure. In the current affidavit, Pizzarelli told investigators that all charges from the 2025 case had been dropped. Weinberger, running for reelection, faced intimidation in 2024 Weinberger, a first-term Republican, represents Florida House District 94 in Palm Beach County, according to the Florida House. Weinberger’s campaign faced a separate voter intimidation case during the 2024 election. Nicholas Farley was arrested after a campaign volunteer said he yelled antisemitic slurs at her and drove threateningly near early voters outside the Acreage Branch Library. Farley told detectives that seeing Weinberger campaign posters triggered his remarks. The case involved Farley, not Pizzarelli. Absolutely it’s very scary we’re dealing with this. It’s just no way to live and maybe he opens his eyes and realize that we’re just all people doesn’t matter your religion or skin color, Weinberger said at the time. Weinberger is seeking reelection on Tuesday. She faces Democrat Elizabeth Holmes and Doug Barrow (no party affiliation). Related: Early voting ends this weekend across Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast She was behind the bill that pushed to rename PBIA in honor of President Donald Trump. House District 94 is entirely within Palm Beach County. It stretches from the western Glades communities of Belle Glade, Pahokee and South Bay through areas such as Westlake, Loxahatchee Groves, The Acreage and Jupiter Farms, and includes parts of several eastern communities, including West Palm Beach, Palm Beach Gardens, Jupiter and Royal Palm Beach.

entry.summary: After securing their first win against the New York Jets last Sunday , the Miami Dolphins locker room has new energy. 'I think we did a good job celebrating as a team in the locker room. That's when you have the most excitement and the most joy from going out there and putting it all on the line,' said starting quarterback Malik Willis. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Dolphins turn focus to Patriots after first win Dolphins look to build on first win While the win is a breath of fresh air, the guys know things won't get easier as they prepare to face the New England Patriots on Sunday. 'Division games are important. All these guys watched them play in the Super Bowl last year. I mean, we have 15 rookies, and I hope they all watched the Super Bowl last year, but you never know these days. I'd assume that they all know that the team just went to the Super Bowl,' said head coach Jeff Hafley. The players said they watched the Super Bowl last year, and they're ready for arguably their toughest test of the season. 'It starts today; you know we have to bring our juice today in practice. During the whole week, we have to up our level from last week and just come out and attack them, boys,' said defensive lineman Kenneth Grant. If the intensity on the practice field is any indication, the Dolphins are set to fight and claw against the Pats. The defense looked sharp in their drills, special teams executed well, and Willis and the offense looked poised; speaking of poise, third-year running back Ollie Gordon has been just that since taking over the starting role after De'Von Achane tore his ACL. Gordon has rushed for a touchdown in four straight games and gained 100 yards twice. 'I would say it's huge. I can't do it without my teammates, though; without the line blocking how they are, the tight ends playing how they are, and without our quarterback playing how he is. I come out here and play for my teammates,' Gordon said.

entry.title: King tides swamp Treasure Coast roads as coastal flood warning stretches into Friday - WPEC
entry.summary: King tides swamp Treasure Coast roads as coastal flood warning stretches into Friday    WPEC
entry.article_text: King tides are pushing water onto roads across the Treasure Coast , and forecasters say the high water isn’t done yet. The National Weather Service extended a coastal flood warning for Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties until 2 a.m. The warning first took effect early Sunday and was originally set to expire Monday night. Martin County has taken some of the worst of it. In Sewall’s Point , floodwater has covered streets and made driving dangerous. Indian River Drive is also underwater for long stretches. Martin County officials say flooding has been reported on Southeast MacArthur Boulevard on Hutchinson Island, in Old Palm City and along South Sewall’s Point. The Martin County Sheriff’s Office reported significant flooding in Palm City, including Southwest Dyer Point Road, Southwest 34th Street and Cornell Avenue. King tides are exceptionally high tides that happen around a full or new moon, when the pull of the sun and moon line up and lift the water higher than usual. This round came around Sunday night’s full moon. Strong onshore winds piled even more water against the coast, sending it over seawalls and into low-lying neighborhoods. See also: Corvette, Ferrari take baths as king tides flood West Palm Beach, Lantana Some relief is on the way, but not right away. CBS12 meteorologists expect the winds to ease through the rest of the week. Even with calmer conditions, the tides will stay high enough to keep pushing water into flood-prone streets around high tide. The weather service warns that coastal roads may close and that low-lying homes, businesses and some critical infrastructure could flood. Forecasters also expect significant shoreline erosion. Coastal flooding is occurring or imminent, the weather service said in its latest statement. The beaches remain dangerous as well. A high surf advisory is in effect until 2 a.m. Friday, with breaking waves of 7 to 11 feet. A high rip current risk runs through late Friday night, and forecasters urge swimmers to stay out of the water. Drivers should not go around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

entry.article_text: King tides and strong onshore winds have caused significant coastal erosion along the boardwalk in Vero Beach, with officials describing the damage as severe and warning that the weather event is not yet over. I was trying to look it up to see if there was a name, a named storm off the coast or anything, but nope, it's just weather," one observer said. Quintin Bergman is the resource manager with Indian River County. He's monitoring the situation. "So, what we're seeing here is two weather events that have aligned," Bergman said. "We're still in the middle of this. We're not through with the weather event. The forecast is showing elevated winds for a few more days, and the king tide event is still going to be affecting the tide." The erosion has impacted a section of beachfront parking on Ocean Drive, an area official have identified as one of their erosion hot spots. One couple who walked on the beach the day before said they didn’t notice the damage but weren’t surprised by the situation. "That's what nature wants to do, and that's kind of what you need to let nature do, I think. But the problem is we keep building on it. That's the interruption, not nature doing its thing," they said. Deep Dive: WPBF 25 News Investigates Officials described the erosion as approaching severe. "I would classify this as leaning more on the severe side of erosion. It's not extreme by any means, but definitely we are very concerned," Bergman said. Authorities are contacting park officials to discuss safety measures to protect the public. Lucie County, beach erosion has also been observed, but officials credited beach replenishment projects with helping protect nearby buildings. "I mean, it certainly helped that we did a renourishment last year. Any time you lose sand, the more you have on there, the better you're going to protect your shoreline," Erick Gill, St. Lucie County public information officer, said. In parts of Martin County, residents are still dealing with flooding caused by the rough conditions. Despite the challenges, some beachgoers in Vero Beach, like Svetlana Ryan, are still enjoying the view and noting the changes to the shoreline. "We noticed because there was so much sand before, and now it's just a wall. But you do with whatever you have to do here in Vero Beach," Ryan said. entry.title: Health Department takes another look at St Lucie County glioblastoma cases
entry.summary: ST. LUCIE COUNTY, Fla. Nearly eight years after WPTV first investigated concerns about a possible cluster of glioblastoma cases in St. Lucie County, health officials have reviewed the numbers again. The latest findings show the number of cases remains in line with what would be expected based on the county's population, but families who lost loved ones to the deadly brain cancer say important questions remain unanswered. The latest review by the Florida Department of Health follows years of WPTV reporting into concerns raised by patients and families who discovered they lived near others diagnosed with the same aggressive form of brain cancer. While health officials say the data does not show a statistically significant increase in cases, the review does not examine whether patients were concentrated on particular streets or in specific neighborhoods. For families who have spent years searching for answers, that distinction matters. A young man's death helped spark an investigation For Deb Johnston, the loss of her son, Lenny Schelin Jr., is still painful. 'It's been 8 years since Lenny passed,' she said. Lenny was just 33 years old when he died from glioblastoma, one of the most aggressive forms of brain cancer. He was healthy, active and loved fishing. He survived just 17 months after his diagnosis. 'Everybody loved Lenny. He just had this charm about him,' his mother recalled. Lenny's story was among the first that helped WPTV uncover concerns about glioblastoma cases in St. Lucie County. Other patients included Mark Cunningham, who was also in his 30s, and Kyle Vericella, who was just 18.
