entry.summary: Martin County and Okeechobee County schools closed Tuesday due to flooding    WFLX
entry.article_text: Both Okeechobee County and Martin County Public Schools will be closed Tuesday, Nov. 3, as flooding and severe weather continue to create unsafe travel conditions across the region. MARTIN COUNTY SCHOOLS CLOSED All Martin County School District-operated schools will be closed Tuesday, which will also include all after-school activities. School officials said in a Facebook post that conditions vary significantly across the region, with some communities experiencing serious flooding and difficult travel conditions. The district said many of its employees and families live outside Martin County and commute into the county each day. Those conditions in neighboring communities played an important role in the decision to close schools. Throughout Monday, the district received reports of employees and families driving through floodwaters to get home, abandoning vehicles because of impassable roads and making alternate overnight accommodations because they could not safely remain in their homes. Officials said they also considered whether employees would be able to safely travel to and from campuses and whether schools would have enough staff and resources to safely support students throughout the day. The district said the decision follows Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis' declaration of a state of emergency covering Martin County and surrounding counties. "We encourage everyone to use caution and prioritize their safety as conditions continue to affect our region," the district said. Families are being asked to monitor the Martin County School District's website and social media accounts for additional updates. OKEECHOBEE COUNTY SCHOOLS CLOSED Okeechobee County district officials announced Monday evening that lingering floodwaters continue to make some campuses and bus stops unsafe. In a Facebook post, the district said crews spent Monday assessing school campuses and their accessibility following widespread flooding across the county. Officials had hoped water levels would fall enough to reopen schools Tuesday, but floodwaters were still preventing safe access to some campuses Monday evening. The district also said flooding has created unsafe conditions in several areas where students would normally wait for school buses. After consulting with the Okeechobee County Emergency Operations Center, district officials said there was no guarantee conditions would improve enough overnight to safely reopen. "To avoid further delay and inconvenience to parents and the community, we have determined that keeping schools closed Tuesday is the safest decision for our students, families, and staff," the district said. District teams will continue checking conditions Tuesday and will provide additional information about when schools can reopen. Officials said the district will also announce in the coming days whether any makeup days will be necessary. The continued closure comes after heavy rainfall caused significant flooding across Okeechobee County, leaving neighborhoods underwater and roads difficult to navigate.

entry.title: Indian River, St. Lucie counties declare local states of emergency amid widespread flooding
entry.summary: Indian River and St. Lucie counties declared local states of emergency Monday as heavy rainfall and flooding continued to inundate roads and neighborhoods across the Treasure Coast. In Indian River County, County Administrator John A. Titkanich Jr. issued the emergency order in response to ongoing flooding, deteriorating weather conditions and continued rainfall. The county said numerous roads have become impassable, creating public safety concerns. The Indian River County emergency order took effect at 2:30 p.m. Monday and will remain in effect until further order. County officials said the declaration gives the county authority to take emergency actions, coordinate response efforts and address hazardous conditions as they develop. Indian River County Shelter Openings Shelters are open Monday night at these two locations: Sebastian River Middle School, located at 9400 Co Rd 512 in Sebastian Osceola Magnet School (formerly Osceola Middle School), located at 480 20th Ave SW, Vero Beach. This location is a pet-friendly shelter Report non-emergency flooding or property damage through our online reporting portal at IndianRiver.gov. For information or questions, call 772-226-4000. In St. Lucie County, officials also declared a local state of emergency Monday afternoon to expedite access to any additional resources that may be needed as flooding affects streets and neighborhoods. St. Lucie County's Emergency Operations Center is operating under a Level 2 partial activation. Public Safety personnel are coordinating with law enforcement, water management agencies and local governments in response to the flooding. Officials are asking residents to refrain from traveling Monday evening if possible and warning motorists not to attempt to drive through flooded roads. Crews are working to address problems across St. Lucie County as several streets and neighborhoods experience flooding. The City of Port St. Lucie also declared a state of emergency in alignment with the county. The City Council was scheduled to meet Tuesday at 1 p.m. at City Hall to vote to formally approve the State of Emergency, which can help expedite any additional resources as needed. For information or questions, call 772-226-4000.In St. Lucie County, officials also declared a local state of emergency Monday afternoon to expedite access to any additional resources that may be needed as flooding affects streets and neighborhoods.St. Lucie County's Emergency Operations Center is operating under a Level 2 partial activation. Public Safety personnel are coordinating with law enforcement, water management agencies and local governments in response to the flooding.Officials are asking residents to refrain from traveling Monday evening if possible and warning motorists not to attempt to drive through flooded roads.Crews are working to address problems across St. Lucie County as several streets and neighborhoods experience flooding.The City of Port St. Lucie also declared a state of emergency in alignment with the county. The City Council was scheduled to meet Tuesday at 1 p.m. at City Hall to vote to formally approve the State of Emergency, which can help expedite any additional resources as needed.Indian River County issued a similar warning, urging residents to avoid unnecessary travel through flood-affected areas, obey road closures and barricades and never attempt to drive through flooded roadways. The Florida Department of Health in St. Lucie County is also warning residents about potential health hazards associated with floodwaters.Health officials advise residents to avoid eating or drinking anything contaminated with floodwater and to avoid contact with floodwater, particularly if they have open cuts or sores.People who have wounds exposed to floodwater should thoroughly wash the affected area with soap and seek medical care if redness, swelling or drainage develops.Residents with flooded private wells are being advised that heavy rainfall could make their water unsafe to drink. Those who aren't sure whether flooding has affected their well should use bottled or boiled water for drinking, making ice, brushing their teeth and cleaning cuts or injuries.Health officials also said people with septic systems experiencing slow plumbing should conserve water and avoid having their septic tanks pumped while groundwater levels remain exceptionally high.Both counties are asking residents to continue monitoring official sources as conditions change.Indian River County said protecting residents, visitors and emergency responders remains a priority and encouraged the public to monitor official county communications for further updates.

entry.title: Brightline temporarily suspends service between Orlando and West Palm Beach due to high water
entry.summary: Brightline temporarily suspended train service between Orlando and West Palm Beach because of high water along its rail corridor in Brevard County. The rail company said maintenance crews are at the scene and service will not resume until Tuesday at 8:30 p.m. Brightline said its rail infrastructure teams are monitoring conditions along the corridor in coordination with Florida East Coast Railway. Once water levels recede, crews will inspect tracks, signals and crossings in the affected area before passenger trains are allowed to resume service. Service between Miami, Aventura, Fort Lauderdale, Boca Raton and West Palm Beach is operating normally, according to the company. Passengers with reservations affected by the suspension will be contacted directly about their travel options. Brightline is encouraging passengers to check its website, mobile app and social media channels for the latest service information. The disruption comes as heavy rain affects parts of Florida's east coast, bringing flooding concerns to portions of the state.

entry.title: NTSB: Learjet 60 crew reported icing, turbulence shortly before deadly Palm Beach County crash
entry.summary: The crew of a Learjet that crashed in Palm Beach County on Sunday reported icing, moderate turbulence and precipitation minutes before the aircraft rapidly descended and crashed, killing all nine people aboard, federal investigators said Monday. During a Monday afternoon news conference, National Transportation Safety Board Member Tom Chapman laid out a preliminary timeline of the Learjet 60's final flight and said weather conditions will be a major focus of the investigation. WATCH INVESTIGATIVE REPORTER KATE HUSSEY'S REPORT BELOW: Weather may have played role in Florida Learjet crash, NTSB says Investigators also have some evidence that the aircraft began breaking apart before impact, although Chapman stressed the NTSB is still working to determine exactly what happened. The Learjet 60 was operated by Aurora Aviation doing business as Upper Jets, according to Chapman. The plane left Austin-Bergstrom International Airport at approximately 10:37 a.m. ET Sunday, bound for North Eleuthera in the Bahamas. There were nine people aboard, including two flight crew members and seven passengers. The NTSB said at approximately 12:47 p.m., the crew told air traffic controllers they were encountering light clear icing that they considered manageable, along with moderate turbulence. The aircraft was flying at 35,000 feet when the crew reported altitude deviations of approximately 700 feet. They also reported an outside temperature of minus 53 degrees Fahrenheit. WATCH THE NTSB news conference below: NTSB holds news conference on Learjet crash in Palm Beach County Shortly afterward, the crew reported encountering precipitation and asked to climb to 37,000 feet. Air traffic control approved the request. 'Less than 30 seconds later, a transmission from the airplane announced the descent, followed by a mayday call,' Chapman said. At about 12:48 p.m., investigators said the crew reported the aircraft was in an overspeed condition and descending. Later communications indicated it was rapidly losing altitude. The plane crashed at approximately 12:51 p.m. near Greenacres and Palm Springs. All nine people aboard were killed. Allan Filgueiras confirmed to NBC News that his daughter, Nathalia Filgueiras, 20, was serving as the co-pilot on the deadly flight. entry.article_text: The crew of a Learjet that crashed in Palm Beach County on Sunday reported icing, moderate turbulence and precipitation minutes before the aircraft rapidly descended and crashed, killing all nine people aboard, federal investigators said Monday.During a Monday afternoon news conference, National Transportation Safety Board Member Tom Chapman laid out a preliminary timeline of the Learjet 60's final flight and said weather conditions will be a major focus of the investigation.WATCH INVESTIGATIVE REPORTER KATE HUSSEY'S REPORT BELOW:Investigators also have some evidence that the aircraft began breaking apart before impact, although Chapman stressed the NTSB is still working to determine exactly what happened.The Learjet 60 was operated by Aurora Aviation doing business as Upper Jets, according to Chapman.The plane left Austin-Bergstrom International Airport at approximately 10:37 a.m. ET Sunday, bound for North Eleuthera in the Bahamas. There were nine people aboard, including two flight crew members and seven passengers.The NTSB said at approximately 12:47 p.m., the crew told air traffic controllers they were encountering light clear icing that they considered manageable, along with moderate turbulence.The aircraft was flying at 35,000 feet when the crew reported altitude deviations of approximately 700 feet. They also reported an outside temperature of minus 53 degrees Fahrenheit.WATCH THE NTSB news conference below:Shortly afterward, the crew reported encountering precipitation and asked to climb to 37,000 feet. Air traffic control approved the request."Less than 30 seconds later, a transmission from the airplane announced the descent, followed by a mayday call," Chapman said.At about 12:48 p.m., investigators said the crew reported the aircraft was in an overspeed condition and descending. Later communications indicated it was rapidly losing altitude.The plane crashed at approximately 12:51 p.m. near Greenacres and Palm Springs.All nine people aboard were killed. Allan Filgueiras confirmed to NBC News that his daughter, Nathalia Filgueiras, 20, was serving as the co-pilot on the deadly flight.Chapman said investigators are examining whether the icing and turbulence played a role in the crash.WATCH BELOW: Gov. DeSantis speaks about tragedy"The weather conditions are a major focus of the investigation," Chapman said, adding that investigators still need to determine what conditions were like at the plane's cruising altitude.The NTSB has not yet confirmed whether the aircraft flew through an active thunderstorm.Chapman said investigators have "some indication that the aircraft was breaking before impact," but cautioned that the investigation remains in its early stages.The debris field was described as roughly a half-mile by four-tenths of a mile, with debris found around ball fields, businesses and residences.Investigators have not yet identified all of the aircraft pieces recovered from the scene.NTSB Investigator-in-Charge Timothy Monville said one person on the ground suffered a leg injury. The person had been inside a vehicle leaving the area immediately adjacent to the crash site, according to information provided to investigators.Investigators are also trying to determine whether a cockpit voice recorder was aboard the aircraft when it crashed.Chapman said maintenance records indicate one had been installed, but investigators still need to confirm it remained aboard the plane.If recovered, Chapman said information from the recorder could become an important part of the investigation.About 20 NTSB investigators began arriving in Palm Beach County Sunday evening, with additional personnel arriving Monday.The investigative team includes specialists in aircraft systems and structures, recorders, weather and air traffic control, as well as a drone pilot.Monville said one of the biggest challenges will be recovering the main wreckage from the impact crater in the roadway. Water in the crater following heavy rainfall is complicating access to the wreckage.Investigators expect their work at the scene to continue for several days.The NTSB is asking anyone who witnessed the crash or has relevant photographs or video to contact investigators at witness@ntsb.gov. Anyone who finds aircraft debris is being asked not to move it and instead contact authorities.Chapman emphasized that investigators will not determine the probable cause while working at the scene."Our mission is to understand not just what happened, but why it happened and to recommend changes to prevent it from happening again," Chapman said.

entry.article_text: Because of days of consistent rainfall in Palm Beach, Martin, Okeechobee, St. Lucie and Indian River counties that led to flooding, officials have either closed roads or told travelers to avoid roads. OKEECHOBEE COUNTY Highway 78 East closure: Highway 78 East road closure will occur at the 1600 block to allow crews to place a pump capable of moving up to 25,000 gallons of water per minute. The Okeechobee County Sheriff’s Office has established a traffic plan with signs directing motorists to detours. Additional law enforcement officers are en route to assist with traffic control. PALM BEACH COUNTY WEST PALM BEACH: The West Palm Beach Police Department advises travelers to avoid Village Boulevard and 45th Street, Haverhill Road and Tyler Lakes Boulevard, Cumberland Drive and Military Trail, 45th Street and Military Trail, Shenandoah Drive and Military Trail. TOWN OF PALM BEACH: South Ocean Boulevard is closed due to flooding from the 1200 block to the 2200 block of South Ocean Blvd. The town asks travelers to avoid the area. RIVIERA BEACH: The City of Riviera Beach is advising residents and motorists to avoid the intersection of Garden Road and Blue Heron Boulevard due to a water main break. Crews are working to complete repairs, which are expected to be finished by 6 a.m. Please use alternate routes and exercise caution when traveling near the affected area. BOYNTON BEACH: The area from Gateway Boulevard and Seacrest Boulevard to the 1900 block of North Seacrest Boulevard is currently experiencing severe flooding. Motorists are urged to avoid the area and seek alternate routes until conditions improve. Please use caution and never attempt to drive through flooded roadways. BOCA RATON: The city of Boca Raton said on Monday evening that the heavy rains produced standing water in several areas of the city, including: NW Second Avenue and NW 28th Street NW Second Avenue and NW 35th Street Multiple areas of Dixie Highway NW Second Ave from NW 20th Street to Yamato Road The city added that other major roadways across the city are impacted as well, and city staff are actively monitoring the situation. Calls for service are being handled without interruption. LANTANA: Due to heavy rainfall this evening, the Town is experiencing isolated flooding in several areas. Residents are encouraged to stay off the roads and avoid unnecessary travel until conditions improve. Please use caution and do not drive through flooded streets. LAKE PARK: The town of Lake Park said that the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office advises all motorists to avoid Congress Avenue until further notice due to hazardous flooding conditions. The town also asks motorists to avoid Water Tower Road as the road is flooded. 2, at 7 p.m., the following major roadways are closed, with many smaller streets around Port St. Lucie also closed: The intersection of California and Savona boulevards Port St. Lucie Boulevard and Aviation Avenue Eastbound Prima Vista Boulevard, west of Airoso Boulevard. Lucie County has closed westbound Prima Vista Boulevard, east of Airoso Boulevard. The following roadways are being monitored for potential road closings: St. Lucie West Boulevard Becker Road and Savona Boulevard The Florida Department of Transportation is asking that drivers take an alternate route to avoid Port St. Lucie Boulevard from Parr Drive to Alcantarra Boulevard due to water on the roadway and potholes. INDIAN RIVER COUNTY The Indian River County Government said on Monday that 58th Avenue SW between 13th Street SW and 17th Street SW is closed because the road was subject to a washout. The road is closed until further notice. Access to property owners, as well as emergency services, will be maintained at all times. VERO BEACH AREA: 1st St SW – 5200 block 8th Ave at 21st St 12th St – 3500 and 3600 blocks 12th St at 42nd Avenue 16th Ave – 1200 block 17th St – 2200 block 17th St at 6th Avenue 17th Place SW – 1000 block (10th Ave to 17th Place SW) 20th St / SR 60 – 2700 to 3600 blocks 21st Place SW – 1700 to 2000 blocks 26th Court SW – 1400 block 41st Ave – 1000 block 59th Terrace at 57th St 74th Ave – 9th St SW to 1st St SW 82nd Ave – 2500 block 101st Ave – 78th St to CR 512 102nd Court – 8800 block 104th Ave – 83rd St to 85th St Calcutta Dr at Golfview Dr Concha Dr – 700 block CR 512 – 10100 block Highland Dr SW at 21st St SW Main St – 300 block Melrose Lane at CR 512 Sunrise Dr at Village Green Dr U.S. 1 – 8300 to 8500 blocks SEBASTIAN AREA: Autumn Terrace at Melrose Lane Bevan Dr Fischer Hammock Rd – 600 block Periwinkle Dr – 400 block Rolling Hill Dr – 700 block Roseland Rd – 11800 block Roseland Rd at Valencia S. Wimbrow Dr – 200 block The Indian River County Sheriff's Office asks travelers to avoid the areas, use alternate routes and do not drive through standing water. If you have to travel, allow extra time and slow down. The sheriff's office notes that six inches of moving water can stall a vehicle and 12 inches of water can carry the vehicle away. FELLSMERE: The Fellsmere Police Department said on Monday that all of North Broadway will be closed due to the heavy flooding until further notice. New York Street from Pine to Orange will also remain closed due to flooding. Please avoid these areas until further notice and use alternative routes such as Myrtle Street or other roads. MARTIN COUNTY JENSEN BEACH: The Martin County Sheriff's Office said Green River Parkway is flooded and parts are impassable. STUART: The city of Stuart said road flooding conditions were reported at the following locations: NW Dixie Highway southbound lane heading towards old Roosevelt Bridge Australian/Stuart Ave. Wright Boulevard US 1 northbound, north of Roosevelt Bridge just past Publix, Key West Diner, old LA Fitness, Windemere. entry.summary: Florida governor declares state of emergency for Treasure Coast counties after flooding    WPBF

The scene along 41st Avenue and 12th Street, about a mile from Glendale Elementary School, showed water covering roads, front lawns and driveways. Neighbors said they have never seen flooding this severe in the area before. Residents say the steady rain throughout the day overwhelmed drainage systems, leaving water with nowhere to go but into neighborhood streets and yards. A photo shared by the sheriff's office showed just how high the water rose at one point, with only the roof of an SUV visible above the floodwaters. Authorities have not said whether anyone was inside the vehicle. entry.title: 7 in 10 Americans say the midterms are stressing them out
entry.summary: If election season is causing stress, you're not alone. A survey from LifeStance Health found that 70% of Americans are experiencing at least some stress or anxiety about the midterm elections. Gen Z and millennials were more likely to report being stressed by the election. Only about one-third of respondents said they had a plan in place to protect their mental health on election night. About 37% said they are dreading having political conversations during the upcoming holiday season. RELATED STORY | How officials are preparing for Election Day disruptions including from Trump Mental health experts recommend limiting how often you check election news, getting regular exercise and focusing on things you can control. Concerns extend beyond voters. Growing attention is being paid to the mental health of election workers, who have faced heavy workloads, public criticism and, in some cases, harassment and threats. The Carter Center has developed a mental well-being guide to help election officials recognize trauma, build resilience and access mental health support. The organization says prolonged stress can have serious effects on both physical and mental health. RELATED STORY | Election Day deals include free doughnuts and rides to the polls

entry.title: Record-breaking rainfall in West Palm Beach: totals across the area
entry.summary: Some areas across the region received over a foot of rainfall in a day, with most of it happening in just a 12-hour period. The highest totals were just north of Sebastian, with 19.75' in Palm Bay to almost 2 feet of rain in Grant Valkaria in 24 hours. This exceeds a 1-in-1,000-year rainfall event, which is a .1% chance of this amount of rainfall happening in any given year. Radar estimates that over 20 inches of rain fell between Sunday and Monday in West Palm Beach. All of our official daily records were shattered. West Palm Beach almost tripled its previous daily record. The new record is 7.39'. The previous record was 2.52'. This makes it the 2nd highest rainfall on a November day. The record still stands at 7.41' from November 22, 1984. TREASURE COAST Vero Beach had its 2nd highest rainfall on a November day at 4.91'. The record stands at 4.98' on November 4th, 1982. Fort Pierce had 5.39', nearly doubling the daily record of 2.24' from 1946. This is the third-highest total for a November day. Have we ever seen this much rain in a short period? Just a little south of us, including Fort Lauderdale, Hollywood, and Dania Beach, on April 12, 2023. Showers and thunderstorms repeatedly training over this urban corridor brought rainfall rates of 3-6 inches/hour, and 12-hour amounts exceeding 20 inches. Flash flooding left people stranded in inundated vehicles and homes, while also shutting down a major airport.

entry.article_text: As Americans head to the polls on Election Day, affordability remains one of the top issues on voters' minds. Consumer spending has remained relatively strong despite higher prices, but shoppers and retailers alike are still grappling with uncertainty surrounding inflation, tariffs and changing shopping habits. Brett Rose, retail expert and CEO of United National Consumer Suppliers, said the uncertainty is making it harder for retailers to predict what consumers will buy months from now. "Anytime somebody in DC utters the word tariff right now, there's so much consumer concern and consumer uncertainty, which then translates to retail inventory concerns," Rose said. When retailers cannot accurately forecast demand, it affects both inventory decisions and pricing strategies. Shift toward regional suppliers Rose explained that many retailers are increasingly turning to nontraditional suppliers and looking for merchandise that is already available closer to home. "A lot less stuff coming out of the Far East because they need to find goods that are on the ground," Rose said. The strategy allows retailers to reduce risk and avoid being stuck with products that consumers may not ultimately purchase. It also helps businesses react more quickly in a rapidly changing market. Waiting for tariff refunds Another question facing retailers involves billions of dollars in tariff refunds being returned to importers by the federal government. But Rose said consumers should not expect those refunds to directly translate into lower prices at the checkout counter. RELATED STORY | Strong growth and inflation paints mixed picture of economy days before midterms"A lot of retailers are pushing back on suppliers and saying, 'Great. Glad you're getting the money back. When's our check coming?'" Rose said. Still, he said shoppers may be able to benefit indirectly by paying attention to off-price retailers. When companies overestimate demand and end up with excess inventory, they often sell those products to discount chains such as TJ Maxx, Dollar Tree, and Five Below. "There's a surplus of goods in the market. Off-price retailers take advantage of it," Rose said. "That's where the consumer benefits the most." Buying cycle gets shorter As economic concerns remain front and center on Election Day, Rose said retailers are already adapting to volatility regardless of what happens at the polls. One major shift is a shorter buying cycle. Instead of purchasing products 10 to 12 months in advance, retailers are increasingly buying inventory closer to when it will be sold. RELATED STORY | Midterm elections pit Iowans’ economic struggles against conservative values"You buy Christmas in January. You can't predict in a volatile consumer market what they're going to sell in December and January at the start of the year," Rose said. "A lot of traditional retailers, their buying process has become more like an off-price retailer." The changes, he said, reflect a retail industry that is increasingly focused on flexibility as it navigates an uncertain economic landscape.

entry.title: Martin County and Okeechobee County schools closed Tuesday due to flooding
entry.summary: Both Okeechobee County and Martin County Public Schools will be closed Tuesday, Nov. 3, as flooding and severe weather continue to create unsafe travel conditions across the region. MARTIN COUNTY SCHOOLS CLOSED All Martin County School District-operated schools will be closed Tuesday, which will also include all after-school activities. School officials said in a Facebook post that conditions vary significantly across the region, with some communities experiencing serious flooding and difficult travel conditions. The district said many of its employees and families live outside Martin County and commute into the county each day. Those conditions in neighboring communities played an important role in the decision to close schools. Throughout Monday, the district received reports of employees and families driving through floodwaters to get home, abandoning vehicles because of impassable roads and making alternate overnight accommodations because they could not safely remain in their homes. Officials said they also considered whether employees would be able to safely travel to and from campuses and whether schools would have enough staff and resources to safely support students throughout the day. The district said the decision follows Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis' declaration of a state of emergency covering Martin County and surrounding counties. 'We encourage everyone to use caution and prioritize their safety as conditions continue to affect our region,' the district said. Families are being asked to monitor the Martin County School District's website and social media accounts for additional updates. OKEECHOBEE COUNTY SCHOOLS CLOSED Okeechobee County district officials announced Monday evening that lingering floodwaters continue to make some campuses and bus stops unsafe. In a Facebook post, the district said crews spent Monday assessing school campuses and their accessibility following widespread flooding across the county. entry.summary: Treasure Coast flooding prompts local state of emergency    WPBF
entry.article_text: The Treasure Coast is under a local state of emergency after heavy rains caused severe flooding, leaving neighborhoods submerged, roads impassable and residents struggling to navigate the area. Aerial footage reveals the extent of the flooding, with cars stranded and some vehicles stuck in the rising waters. On Del Rio Boulevard in Port St. Lucie, drivers are being forced to find alternative routes. “This is crazy, the amount of rain we’ve had in the last few weeks, and now the ground is so saturated,” Ryan Murray, a resident, said. Murray has been helping others navigate the flooded streets on his kayak. “I’m just trying to guide them around this car. This lady here got picked up a long time ago. We’ve had several school buses here that we’ve helped out, so we’ve done good. I feel that we’re doing our part,” he said. In one instance, a student was seen nearly swimming home after getting off a school bus. Police are urging residents to avoid driving and stay home as parking lots and other areas remain flooded. Tuesday is Election Day, and some polling locations have been moved due to the floodwaters. Lucie County polling places have relocated due to flooding: Precincts 39 and 52 will move from the Spanish Lakes Country Club clubhouse to Lakewood Park Church, located at 5405 Turnpike Feeder Road in Fort Pierce. In Martin County, Grace Presbyterian Church, 1875 NW Britt Rd, Stuart, FL 34994, has been relocated to the Martin County Supervisor of Elections Office, 135 SE Martin Luther King, Jr. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app.

entry.summary: GALLERY: Flooded Port St. Lucie roads remain hazardous as crews check Creekside homes    WPEC
entry.article_text: Lucie police officers continued monitoring flooded neighborhoods and roads Tuesday morning, helping motorists and responding to calls for service as water levels began to recede in some areas. Lucie Police Department said it extended patrol shifts overnight to keep additional officers available to respond to emergencies. Officers were assessing roadways and neighborhoods at daybreak to identify hazards and determine the extent of the flooding. Aerial footage shared by the department showed significant flooding near SW Savage Boulevard, SW Fairgreen Road and SW Salvatierra Boulevard, where water had spread across residential streets and surrounding areas. Flooding was also affecting roadways and neighborhoods near Tradition Parkway and SW Community Boulevard, as well as Torino Parkway, NW California Boulevard and NW Peacock Boulevard. Police said standing water made travel hazardous in those areas and urged motorists to stay off flooded roads. See also: Flooded roads complicate trip to Port St. Lucie polls; Legacy High School site is open The St. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office drone team is working with the St. Lucie County Fire District to conduct home checks in the Creekside community. Officers continued working throughout the city to assist residents, help stranded motorists, respond to calls and monitor areas affected by rising water. Police asked people to stay home if possible and allow emergency crews to assist those in need. Roads that are flooded, barricaded or significantly impacted Police reported flooding or barricades at these locations: Port St. Lucie Boulevard at Aviation Avenue Northbound Port St. Lucie Boulevard from Dalton Boulevard to Gatlin Boulevard Selvitz Road from Midway Road to Peachtree Boulevard Peachtree Boulevard Westmoreland Boulevard in front of The Anchorage Savona Boulevard and California Boulevard St. Lucie West Boulevard Volusia Drive from Blanton Boulevard to Torino Parkway California Boulevard in front of Fire Station 14 Country Club Estates of St. Lucie West Northbound Cashmere Boulevard Roads where water is receding or has cleared Police said water was beginning to recede on Lennard Road at Melaleuca Boulevard, Hillmoor Drive in front of HCA St. Lucie Medical Center and near the 1700 block, and Village Green Drive. Vehicles could pass on those roads, but four disabled vehicles on Lennard Road were awaiting removal. Flooding had subsided on Becker Road from Hallmark Street to Savona Boulevard, Darwin Boulevard and College Park Road. Several disabled vehicles remained on Becker and Darwin. Flooding had also cleared on Darwin Boulevard at Fifer Avenue, where two disabled vehicles remained. Rosser Boulevard had cleared, but SW Rosser Road at SW Paar Drive and SW Delos Drive remained flooded and impassable. Police reported no flooding on Airoso Boulevard from Lakehurst Boulevard to Eyerly Avenue, though several disabled vehicles in the county jurisdiction were awaiting removal. One disabled vehicle in a turn lane at Port St. Lucie Boulevard and Airoso Boulevard was not significantly impeding traffic. The department cautioned that conditions could change quickly, especially if more rain falls. Police urged drivers to avoid flooded roads, never drive through standing water and stay home unless travel is necessary. Turn Around, Don’t Drown, the department reminded residents. Call 911 to report downed power lines, fallen trees, road obstructions or other hazards that pose an immediate danger.

entry.article_text: Lucie voters assigned to Precinct 90 at Legacy High School can vote there Tuesday, despite flooding and road closures that are making it difficult to reach the polling location, the St. Lucie County Supervisor of Elections office confirmed to CBS12 News. The elections office is directing voters to take Midway Road and Glade Extension to get to the school. CBS12 News had a crew on the scene who said they encountered flooding and roadblocks on Southwest Village Parkway earlier Tuesday and had to turn around. Police had blocked that entrance, but voters could reach Legacy High School by taking an alternate route. The flooding and changing information about the polling location caused confusion for some voters. CBS12 News Paige Meyer reported that voters were being directed to Tradition Town Hall, though it could take a couple of hours to get the site ready. See also: Florida Amendment 3: What a yes or no vote means for homeowners and local services Voter Tommy Sharpe said he was directed there but was told he could not vote because it was not his assigned precinct. He said he was then told Legacy was open and he would need to take a back route. Sharpe said the detour to Legacy would add 20 to 35 minutes to his drive. Voters who cannot reach Legacy High School can go to the Tradition office at 10-267 Southwest Village Parkway, where election staff can print a vote-by-mail ballot. Voters can complete and sign the ballot and return it as directed by staff, the elections office said. Lucie voters are choosing the city’s next mayor Tuesday. entry.title: Collins' office vandalized as she faces tight reelection fight
entry.summary: A Maine office for U.S. Sen. Susan Collins was vandalized in the hours leading up to Tuesday's election, her office said. It was the second reported act of vandalism at her Biddeford office. Officials have not said if anyone has been arrested or charged in connection to the incident. Collins' office released a photo indicating someone sprayed 'BLOOD ON HER HANDS' in red paint. 'This is another incident in a series and the second attempt at our Biddeford office to intimidate the Senator and her staff. These tactics are disturbing, but not effective. Our staff is undeterred and on the job,' Collins' chief of staff, Katie Brown, said in a statement. RELATED STORY | All eyes on Maine as critical Senate race draws closer Collins is in the midst of a tight reelection bid against Democrat Troy Jackson. Several polls in recent days have shown Jackson opening a narrow lead over Collins. She is seeking a sixth term in the Senate. Even in years when Maine has favored Democrats, Collins has won reelection by comfortable margins. For Republicans to retain control of the Senate, Collins' reelection is seen as imperative. With President Donald Trump's approval rating slowly declining, Collins has sought to distance herself from Trump in recent months. She has reminded voters that she was among seven Republicans who voted to convict Trump in his second impeachment trial in 2021. entry.article_text: Lucie police officers continued monitoring flooded neighborhoods and roads Tuesday morning, helping motorists and responding to calls for service as water levels began to recede in some areas. Lucie Police Department said it extended patrol shifts overnight to keep additional officers available to respond to emergencies. Officers were assessing roadways and neighborhoods at daybreak to identify hazards and determine the extent of the flooding. Aerial footage shared by the department showed significant flooding near SW Savage Boulevard, SW Fairgreen Road and SW Salvatierra Boulevard, where water had spread across residential streets and surrounding areas. Flooding was also affecting roadways and neighborhoods near Tradition Parkway and SW Community Boulevard, as well as Torino Parkway, NW California Boulevard and NW Peacock Boulevard. Police said standing water made travel hazardous in those areas and urged motorists to stay off flooded roads. See also: Flooded roads complicate trip to Port St. Lucie polls; Legacy High School site is open The St. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office drone team is working with the St. Lucie County Fire District to conduct home checks in the Creekside community. Officers continued working throughout the city to assist residents, help stranded motorists, respond to calls and monitor areas affected by rising water. Police asked people to stay home if possible and allow emergency crews to assist those in need. Roads that are flooded, barricaded or significantly impacted Police reported flooding or barricades at these locations: Port St. Lucie Boulevard at Aviation Avenue Northbound Port St. Lucie Boulevard from Dalton Boulevard to Gatlin Boulevard Selvitz Road from Midway Road to Peachtree Boulevard Peachtree Boulevard Westmoreland Boulevard in front of The Anchorage Savona Boulevard and California Boulevard St. Lucie West Boulevard Volusia Drive from Blanton Boulevard to Torino Parkway California Boulevard in front of Fire Station 14 Country Club Estates of St. Lucie West Northbound Cashmere Boulevard Roads where water is receding or has cleared Police said water was beginning to recede on Lennard Road at Melaleuca Boulevard, Hillmoor Drive in front of HCA St. Lucie Medical Center and near the 1700 block, and Village Green Drive. Vehicles could pass on those roads, but four disabled vehicles on Lennard Road were awaiting removal. Flooding had subsided on Becker Road from Hallmark Street to Savona Boulevard, Darwin Boulevard and College Park Road. Several disabled vehicles remained on Becker and Darwin. Flooding had also cleared on Darwin Boulevard at Fifer Avenue, where two disabled vehicles remained. Rosser Boulevard had cleared, but SW Rosser Road at SW Paar Drive and SW Delos Drive remained flooded and impassable. Police reported no flooding on Airoso Boulevard from Lakehurst Boulevard to Eyerly Avenue, though several disabled vehicles in the county jurisdiction were awaiting removal. One disabled vehicle in a turn lane at Port St. Lucie Boulevard and Airoso Boulevard was not significantly impeding traffic. The department cautioned that conditions could change quickly, especially if more rain falls. Police urged drivers to avoid flooded roads, never drive through standing water and stay home unless travel is necessary. Turn Around, Don’t Drown, the department reminded residents. Call 911 to report downed power lines, fallen trees, road obstructions or other hazards that pose an immediate danger.

OKEECHOBEE COUNTY Highway 78 East closure: Highway 78 East road closure will occur at the 1600 block to allow crews to place a pump capable of moving up to 25,000 gallons of water per minute. The Okeechobee County Sheriff’s Office has established a traffic plan with signs directing motorists to detours. Additional law enforcement officers are en route to assist with traffic control. PALM BEACH COUNTY WEST PALM BEACH: The West Palm Beach Police Department advises travelers to avoid Village Boulevard and 45th Street, Haverhill Road and Tyler Lakes Boulevard, Cumberland Drive and Military Trail, 45th Street and Military Trail, Shenandoah Drive and Military Trail. TOWN OF PALM BEACH: South Ocean Boulevard is closed due to flooding from the 1200 block to the 2200 block of South Ocean Blvd. The town asks travelers to avoid the area. RIVIERA BEACH: The City of Riviera Beach is advising residents and motorists to avoid the intersection of Garden Road and Blue Heron Boulevard due to a water main break. Crews are working to complete repairs, which are expected to be finished by 6 a.m. Please use alternate routes and exercise caution when traveling near the affected area. BOYNTON BEACH: The area from Gateway Boulevard and Seacrest Boulevard to the 1900 block of North Seacrest Boulevard is currently experiencing severe flooding. Motorists are urged to avoid the area and seek alternate routes until conditions improve. Please use caution and never attempt to drive through flooded roadways. LAKE PARK: The town of Lake Park said that the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office advises all motorists to avoid Congress Avenue until further notice due to hazardous flooding conditions. Her platform calls for a statewide rent freeze, a $30 minimum wage, single-payer health care, and public ownership of the energy grid.She is running outside the Democratic Party on purpose. “I don’t think we need to hide it anymore,” Kubicek said.“Whether you want to call it a labor party, a socialist party, a workers party, something that is owned and controlled by working people rather than the Democratic Party establishment or in whatever state, Republican establishment or whatever it might be, something that working people are actually in charge of is what we're trying to build,” she added.Her campaign highlights a growing focus on where the DSA movement can go next. Most DSA-backed candidates, however, continue to run as Democrats.Many won their Democratic primaries that way. In Providence, DSA-backed David Morales ousted incumbent Mayor Brett Smiley. In Colorado, Melat Kiros beat longtime Rep. In New York, Darializa Avila Chevalier unseated five-term incumbent Rep. Adriano Espaillat.Kiros and Avila Chevalier are among five DSA-backed House candidates seeking to join returning Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Rashida Tlaib in Congress. Seven DSA-aligned congressional candidates are running in heavily Democratic districts and could produce the movement’s largest contingent in CongressMichael Kazin, a Georgetown University historian who has studied the American left, told Scripps News socialism “is gaining ground especially among Democrats and especially in very blue areas.” He noted that DSA members in Congress “are all in very safe seats.”IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | Democratic Socialists become a rising force in Democratic politicsYounger voters remain central to the movement’s rise. A Pew Research Center survey found 39% of Democrats under 30 view democratic socialist leaders favorably, compared with 26% of those 50 and older.Sara Almosawi, a former national co-chair of the Young Democratic Socialists of America, told Scripps News, “A lot of young people are very much down for DSA.”“Young people are flocking towards democratic socialism because we're willing to take a stand on the billionaire-class to take a stand on Palestine, on the affordability crisis,” Almosawi said.“Political power is built from the bottom up,” she said, referring to DSA candidates running for local offices. “We can build a bench that is ready to take on much more significant political power.”Both Almosawi and Kaznin pointed out the need for democratic socialists in office to build coalitions among Democrats and Republicans.“At the end of the day I still want us to be building working class power, and we need to do what it takes to get there and with a small block, we can't just do that alone,” Almosawi said."Every party to become a majority party in this country has to be a big tent,” Kazin said.Kazin said the movement’s long-term appeal will depend on effective governing. He pointed to the early 20th century “sewer socialism” in Milwaukee when socialist officials won support by delivering basic services.“It depends on how well Socialists govern in the end,” he said. “That is the litmus test.”Tuesday also brings tests of DSA-backed candidates outside Congress. For Kubicek, the stakes go beyond one seat and Election night.“We’ve talked to thousands of people about socialism,” she said. “Now let’s show them what a socialist is really about -- win, lose or draw.”

entry.article_text: Severe flooding along the Treasure Coast has led to several school closures as districts await for conditions to clear. The Martin County School District is reviewing weather impacts and safe conditions before deciding whether schools will operate Wednesday, Nov. Currently, schools within the school district are closed Tuesday, November 3 due to the onslaught of flooding. The district said it will share an update on Wednesday’s schedule as soon as possible after the assessment. It recognized that families and employees are making plans and said the safety and well-being of students, staff and families remain its priority. Lucie schools to close Wednesday as flooding continues The St. Lucie County School District is making its community and students the main concern when it comes to flooding conditions surrounding the schools. On Tuesday, Superintendent Dr. Prince announced the school would be closed on Wednesday. entry.title: Heavy rain floods Port St. Lucie roads, strands drivers; residents call for drainage improvements - WPTV

entry.article_text: Heavy rain is flooding roadways across the Treasure Coast, leaving drivers stranded, disrupting daily routines and prompting police to urge residents to stay off the roads unless travel is absolutely necessary.WATCH OUR COVERAGE HERE: Along Southwest Airoso Boulevard in Port St. Lucie, floodwaters reached approximately knee-deep in some areas, turning roadways into lakes and covering sidewalks. Vehicles that attempted to drive through the water stalled, leaving drivers waiting for help as passing cars sent waves toward already stranded vehicles.Port St. Lucie police say officers are responding to a significant number of calls involving vehicles stranded in floodwaters.One driver told WPTV his vehicle died while he was trying to pick up his children."I'm on hold with the insurance company right now trying to get some help," he said.The man, who has lived in the area for six years, said he believes drainage conditions have gotten worse following heavy rain events.Another woman found herself stranded after her vehicle stopped working just minutes after driving toward Southwest Airoso Boulevard."Every time a car comes by, it pushes my car," she told WPTV.The woman could only speak to WPTV through a small opening in her driver's side door as water continued to rush toward her vehicle. A nearby man eventually tried to help her get out.A couple nearby also described watching their vehicle sink deeper into the floodwaters after being stranded for about an hour, with waves from passing traffic pushing the car around.WATCH BELOW: Aerial video of flooding in St. Lucie WestFor some residents, the flooding created more than just a driving hazard. It also raised concerns about getting children to and from school.One woman told WPTV she was trying to figure out how to pick up her children after parents were notified they needed to retrieve their students."They just announced it, they just called parents right now to pick up kids from school. They let the kids go to school knowing it was like this," she said.She said her sister lost a nearly new vehicle to flooding on the same road just last year."It was only three months old, and she got stuck here on the road because the drainage system here sucks, is so bad," she said.The woman questioned whether the city's road expansion efforts are being matched with improvements to its drainage infrastructure."They just keep widening the roads, not even worried about anything else," she said.The city says it is working on longer-term drainage improvements, including a project in the Oak Hammock neighborhood.Plans include new retention ponds, drainage boxes and raising portions of California Boulevard and Savona Boulevard to help address recurring flooding.However, the project remains in the data-collection phase and could take years to complete.In the meantime, the city says it is testing water-level sensors to help crews respond more quickly to flooding and working to clear debris from drainage systems.Crews are also checking drainage systems for water flow and addressing potholes reported or discovered during inspections.Port St. Lucie police are asking residents to stay home and avoid traveling unless absolutely necessary.Officials warn that even a few inches of moving water can be dangerous and remind drivers never to underestimate the depth or current of floodwaters.

Friends are convinced it was Gregory, a devout Christian.A federal investigator said Monday that parts of the jet likely started to break off before it struck the ground. Gregory’s co-pilot, 20-year-old Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, told air traffic controllers that ice was accumulating on the plane and that severe turbulence had thrown it up and down by more than 700 feet (210 meters).“We’re going to die!” she said with a scream before the jet slammed into the ground and erupted in a fireball.Thomas Noetzel, the director of operations at the company that operated the flight, Upper Jets, organized an online fundraiser to support Gregory’s wife and children.Gregory was a close, personal friend and “knowing him has made me a better person,” Noetzel wrote on the fundraising website GoFundMe.“Jeff was a devoted, conscientious, and deeply faithful man who had a genuine passion for flying and a strong love for the Lord ,” Noetzel’s father, Walter, posted on Facebook. “His journey on earth may have ended, but I like to think he is now flying among the angels, soaring peacefully in the presence of our Lord.”Gregory held airline transport pilot and flight instructor certificates, according to Federal Aviation Administration records. He lived in Gilbertsville, about 35 miles (56 kilometers) northwest of Philadelphia, and had previously worked for a charter company based in Allentown, Pennsylvania.“We are deeply saddened to learn that Captain Jeff Gregory was among those who lost their lives,” said April Honnen, the director of charter sales for East Coast Jets, Inc., where he worked in 2016 and 2017. “Our prayers go out to Jeff’s family, his fellow crew member, the passengers and everyone affected by this heart breaking tragedy.”The Learjet hit the ground with enough force to create a crater before bursting into flames. The impact scattered plane fragments over a large area.Images of the moment just before the aircraft made impact appear to show the horizontal stabilizer missing from the tail. About 600 nearby residents remain displaced, but only one injury was reported on the ground.The plane took off from Austin, Texas. The victims included technology entrepreneur Adam Robinson, his wife, Helen Sharp, and their two young children, relatives said.Filgueiras' stepfather, Thiago Corteleti, told the New York Post that she texted her boyfriend about 10 minutes before the crash, telling him: “I’ve got turbulence, I’ve got ice.”The texts were sent before the situation became critical. In the last two minutes of the flight, Filgueiras shifted from calmly communicating with air traffic controllers to calling out terrifying updates as the plane plummeted.The FAA prohibits commercial airline pilots from using cellphones at any point during a flight. The rules aren’t as strict for pilots of charter flights; they are not supposed to use cellphones during critical phases of flight, such as takeoffs and landings, but are allowed while cruising at altitude unless their company or pilot in command specifically bans it.Tom Chapman, a National Transportation Safety Board member, said Monday that weather would be a key focus of the investigation. entry.summary: The City of Riviera Beach is holding a press conference on flood and storm conditions on Tuesday at 3:30 p.m. to address flooding, road closures and emergency response efforts. Mayor Douglas Lawson and city officials are briefing the public on the city's response to ongoing flooding and steps residents can take to stay safe. WATCH LIVE: The city said it has activated its Emergency Operations Center to Level 2 in response to heavy rain and street flooding across western Riviera Beach. City departments and emergency crews are coordinating closely to protect residents and restore safe conditions as quickly as possible. As part of the response, the city said crews safely extracted more than 50 residents from the Lone Pine community . Six pumps are currently moving floodwater out of affected neighborhoods and into local canals, and city teams continue to monitor conditions and respond to reports of flooding and damage throughout the area. entry.summary: With voters deciding thousands of races across the country on Tuesday, keeping track of which races to watch throughout the night and when to expect results can get tricky. Here's a rundown of the biggest races hour by hour, along with some clues as to how long it will take to count the votes. All times are in Eastern Standard Time. 6 p.m. The first polls of the night will close in most of Indiana and Kentucky, but no statewide winners will be declared in either state until the last polls close at 7 p.m. Its possible to see winners declared in the states easternmost congressional districts. Key contests in this hour include competitive U.S. House races in Indiana's 5th and Kentucky's 6th congressional districts. 7 p.m. and 7:30 p.m. All polls close at 7 p.m. in six states, including Georgia, South Carolina and Virginia, which tend to complete almost all of their vote counting on election night. In the 2024 general election, the vote count in all three states reached the halfway mark in the 8 p.m. hour. The counts were 90% complete at 10:21 p.m. in Georgia, 11:14 p.m. in South Carolina and 12:07 a.m. in Virginia. In Georgias competitive presidential contest, The Associated Press declared Republican Donald Trump the winner at 12:58 a.m. Most Florida polls will also close at 7 p.m., including in every competitive congressional district, but no statewide winners will be declared until polls in the Central Time Zone close at 8 p.m. Polls in North Carolina, Ohio and West Virginia close at 7:30 p.m. All three states also count votes relatively quickly, reaching the halfway point at around 9 p.m. in 2024 and about 90% in the 11 p.m. hour. The AP declared a winner in Ohios competitive 2024 U.S. Senate race at 11:27 p.m. Some key contests to watch in this hour are U.S. Senate races in Georgia, South Carolina, North Carolina and Ohio; gubernatorial races in Georgia and Ohio; and U.S. House races in Florida, Indiana, South Carolina, Virginia, Ohio and North Carolina. gubernatorial races in Florida and Pennsylvania; and U.S. House races in Alabama, Maine, Michigan, New Hampshire, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Texas.9 p.m.This is election night’s other big logjam, with all polls closing in 15 states, including the midterm battlegrounds of Arizona, Iowa, Kansas, Michigan, Minnesota, Nebraska, New York, Texas and Wisconsin.The 2024 general election vote counts in Iowa, Nebraska, New York and Wisconsin all reached the halfway mark roughly in the 10 p.m. hour, while Minnesota reached 50% of all votes counted at 11:29 p.m. Iowa and New York completed 90% of the count just before midnight, while Minnesota, Nebraska and Wisconsin reached 90% early the next day between 2 and 3:30 a.m.Kansas, Michigan and Texas all begin releasing votes in the 8 p.m. hour, but Michigan trailed the other two in the 2024 vote count. entry.title: Election stress is real: A psychiatrist shares how to protect your mental health
entry.summary: The weight of election season is turning into real stress for many people. Political tension, non-stop headlines, ads and uncertainty can take a toll, but mental health experts say understanding why and knowing what tools to use can help combat it. 2026 midterm election results | Key races for Senate, House and governor According to the American Psychological Association, 69% of adults in the U.S. reported the 2024 presidential election was a significant source of stress. For many voters like Christy Warren, keeping your sanity through it all has been a challenge. 'You cannot escape it. It's exhausting. It's everyday. It's multiple times a day,' Warren said. From the texts, to the calls, and the ads everywhere, election season can be relentless. 'This particular time has been more aggressive than any I've experienced and that to me creates some anxiety. It's just it feels hateful almost,' Warren said. Dr. Arash Javanbakht, professor of psychiatry at Wayne State University and author of the book 'Afraid: Understanding the Purpose of Fear and Harnessing the Power of Anxiety,' says fear is a powerful tool and there's a reason political messaging leans on it. 'Fear works because fear is one of the most fundamental emotions in us with the job of protecting us. If you perceive danger, if you perceive threat, that becomes the highest priority,' Javanbakht said. Javanbakht says what voters have to do in order to manage their mental health is take back control. 'If I'm sick because of the poisonous food I've been eating, the first step is to stop eating that food. So, as I said, it's hard, but I would say try to avoid as much as possible,' Javanbakht said. RELATED STORY | How officials are preparing for Election Day disruptions including from Trump On top of reducing exposure, he offers three tips. The first is to turn negative emotions into positive action. 'Do something, whether it's going political activism, picking up the phone, or charitable work that helps people that I think are negatively affected by these policies,' Javanbakht said. The second is to maintain normal routines. 'Do your exercise, family activities, the movie you watch together, the dinner you have together. We need these normal activities that anchor us in the reality of life and keep us healthy,' Javanbakht said. The third is to reconnect with others. entry.title: Cost of living, corruption top issues and voters deeply unhappy with Trump: Early election takeaways
entry.summary: President Donald Trump has repeatedly encouraged voters to pretend he's on the ballot this Election Day. He's not, of course. But there is reason to believe that Tuesday's midterms, above all, will be a referendum on his performance over the last two years. History, polling and early voting numbers suggest it could be a difficult night for Trump's Republican Party, though the political map, not to mention a fresh round of gerrymandering, could limit Democratic gains. Voters are in the mood for change, according to the AP Voter Poll, which found that roughly three-quarters of voters say they feel 'angry' or 'dissatisfied' with the way things are going in the country today. Most appear to blame the Trump administration for high costs. About 6 in 10 say higher than usual prices are 'more because of Trump's policies' rather than 'more because of factors outside Trump's control.' RELATED STORY | Americans head to polls in high-stakes 2026 midterm elections Additionally, about 70% of voters want Congress to provide more checks and balances on the presidency. Democrats are looking to win majorities in the House and Senate, which would curb Trump's power after he's faced few limits from a compliant Republican-controlled Congress. Several key governors' offices also are up for grabs. More than 59 million Americans already had voted before Tuesday, but many more ballots will be cast on Election Day, and government watchdog groups worry that Trump and his loyalists could interfere with the voting process. Fearing a worst-case scenario, Democrats and nonpartisan watchdogs have trained tens of thousands of volunteers to monitor polling places. Here's what we're watching Tuesday: Trump said: 'Pretend I'm on the ballot.' What do voters say? The Republican president is trying to defy history, which shows that in almost every modern midterm election the party in the White House has lost seats in Congress sometimes many of them. Democrats certainly hope that's the case this year. The party is optimistic, given Trump's dismal approval ratings and voter concerns about the war with Iran and the surging price of gas and other daily necessities. The AP Voter Poll, an expansive survey of the electorate, suggests most are deeply unhappy with Trump, with roughly 6 in 10 saying they disapprove of how he's handling the presidency. The party is optimistic, given Trump's dismal approval ratings and voter concerns about the war with Iran and the surging price of gas and other daily necessities.The AP Voter Poll, an expansive survey of the electorate, suggests most are deeply unhappy with Trump, with roughly 6 in 10 saying they disapprove of how he's handling the presidency.About 4 in 10 say the economy is the most important issue facing the country, while 3 in 10 say the most important issue is democracy, according to the poll, well above the number who said the same about crime, healthcare and immigration.Trump is betting that his base of white working-class voters, which fueled his presidential victories in 2016 and 2024, can save his Republican allies if they show up in great numbers. Heading into Election Day, however, there are signs that Democrats are more fired up to vote against him and his party.We're about to learn whether Trump and his coalition are still strong enough to stave off a political beatdown. Specifically, look to see whether Hispanic and Black voters and younger people who swung toward Trump two years ago now rebuke him.RELATED STORY | In-person early voting hits record pace for midtermsThe answer will have huge implications in the midterms and the next presidential cycle.It doesn't happen often.Since World War II, the House and Senate have flipped from one party to the other in the same midterm just three times: 1946, 1994 and 2006. The common thread when it does happen is an electorate clamoring for change or broad frustration with the sitting president.This year has both, and Democrats are trying to capitalize on the opportunity.Strategists in both parties believe Democrats are on track to win a majority in the House, where Republicans began the current Congress with a slim margin of 220-215.It's unclear how big of a swing there could be, however.

entry.title: Record gas prices greet Election Day voters as cost of living drives turnout
entry.summary: Voters heading to the polls Tuesday are paying more at the pump than on any Election Day on record. The national average for regular gasoline hit $4.12 a gallon, and diesel reached $6.28, according to GasBuddy . Both are the highest national averages ever recorded on an Election Day. That is the backdrop as Americans decide who controls Congress. And for many voters, the cost of everyday life, from fuel and groceries to housing, is the issue bringing them out. More than 60 million people had already cast a ballot before polls opened Tuesday. That is more early votes than in any previous midterm, said Michael McDonald, a University of Florida political science professor who runs the lab's early voting tracker. 'We beat that number which was about 46 million in 2022 by quite a bit,' McDonald told Scripps News. But the early numbers only tell part of the story. Around half of all votes in recent elections have been cast on Election Day itself. In the handful of states reporting Election Day turnout Tuesday morning, McDonald said it looked closer to typical levels.  The early vote, he said, 'was very big, but the election day turnout's gonna be more normal.' That means it is still too early to know whether 2026 will match 2018, which McDonald noted had the highest midterm turnout rate since 1914. RELATED STORY | Election Day deals include free doughnuts and rides to the polls Meanwhile, flash flooding forced officials to move polling places in seven Florida counties, including Brevard, Palm Beach and St. Lucie, under an executive order from Gov. Ron DeSantis. In Oklahoma, a Sunday tornado damaged a community center in Cimarron County, forcing officials to relocate that polling site. Flooding also hit the Four Corners region, impacting polling places in southwestern Colorado. Christopher Mann, research director at the Center for Election Innovation Research , said officials prepare for these events.  'Election officials plan for these kinds of events because they happen somewhere in the country,' he said. Where governors have declared emergencies, Mann said, some voters can return ballots electronically, a procedure normally limited to military and overseas voters. The Justice Department says it is sending about a thousand election monitors to 126 jurisdictions in all 50 states, calling it its 'largest monitoring effort in history.' Monitors watch for potential violations of federal law and are not allowed to interfere with voting.  Who's watchin

entry.title: Flooding closes Mangonia Park polling location, impacts nearby Goodwill
entry.summary: Heavy flooding caused problems for voters and businesses Tuesday in the Town of Mangonia Park. WPTV reporter Christy Waite went to the area and found water surrounding Mangonia Park Town Hall on East Tiffany Drive. Parking lots looked more like lakes, while water covered a road with a posted speed limit of 25 mph. The flooding forced the polling location inside Town Hall to close. One voter arrived ready to cast her ballot, only to discover the location was no longer open. I had no idea it closed; I didn't know what to do. Thank you for helping me, she said. Voters were instead sent to Bak Middle School of the Arts to cast their ballots. Mangonia Park Town Manager Ken Metcalf told WPTV the small community was hit hard by the flooding. We have a lot of flooding in this neighborhood on Tiffany Lakes, and of course the town hall is in the middle of it, Metcalf said. Despite the weather and last-minute change, Metcalf said he hoped the flooding would not keep people from voting. We did actually catch 3 people here before they closed down and relocated, so we hope it doesn't have an effect, he said. The flooding was not only impacting voters. Just steps away from Town Hall, the neighboring Gulfstream Goodwill Industries was closed and its parking lot was submerged. Waite connected with a Gulfstream Goodwill Industries leader who said the building in Mangonia Park would remain closed until the water recedes. For town leaders, the focus now is on waiting for the floodwaters to go down. We need a lot of sunshine and a lot of patience. It is a waiting game so if we something that will have an impact we will do it, Metcalf said.

entry.title: Plane parts found as far as 3.8 miles from crash site in South Florida, NTSB official says
entry.summary: Investigators found part of the tail of the jet that crashed in Palm Beach County more than a mile from the crater caused when the aircraft made impact. National Transportation Safety Board member Tom Chapman said during a news conference Tuesday that the discovery of tail parts confirms the plane was breaking apart before it hit the ground. Chapman said the tail's elevator was broken into three parts, and without that intact, pilot would not have been able to pull the Learjet out of its nose dive. The function of the elevator is to control the pitch up and down,' he said. 'At those speeds I dont know that it wouldve been effective even if it had still been attached to the aircraft, but knowing that it was lost is a very important piece of evidence in terms of pointing us towards other things to investigate. Chapman acknowledged Monday that parts of the jet likely started to break off before it struck the ground. The co-pilot, Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, told air traffic controllers minutes before the crash that ice was accumulating on the plane and that severe turbulence had thrown it up and down by more than 700 feet. Were going to die! she said with a scream before the jet slammed into the ground and erupted in a fireball. Friends and family celebrate and mourn the pilot Family and friends of one of the pilots have been posting online about the longtime aviator, husband and father from the Philadelphia suburbs. Jeff Gregory, 55, was one of two crew members in the cockpit of the Bahamas-bound Learjet 60 as it encountered bad weather and slammed into the ground Sunday afternoon in Greenacres, about 7 miles southwest of West Palm Beach. As the plane plunged, a mans voice could be heard reciting the Lords Prayer in the background of the copilots final radio transmissions to air traffic control. Friends are convinced it was Gregory, a devout Christian. Thomas Noetzel, the director of operations at the company that operated the flight, Upper Jets, organized an online fundraiser to support Gregorys wife and children. Gregory was a close, personal friend and knowing him has made me a better person, Noetzel wrote on the fundraising website GoFundMe. Jeff was a devoted, conscientious, and deeply faithful man who had a genuine passion for flying and a strong love for the Lord , Noetzels father, Walter, posted on Facebook. entry.article_text: Investigators found part of the tail of the jet that crashed in Palm Beach County more than a mile from the crater caused when the aircraft made impact.National Transportation Safety Board member Tom Chapman said during a news conference Tuesday that the discovery of tail parts confirms the plane was breaking apart before it hit the ground.Chapman said the tail's elevator was broken into three parts, and without that intact, pilot would not have been able to pull the Learjet out of its nose dive.“The function of the elevator is to control the pitch up and down," he said. "At those speeds I don’t know that it would’ve been effective even if it had still been attached to the aircraft, but knowing that it was lost is a very important piece of evidence in terms of pointing us towards other things to investigate.”Chapman acknowledged Monday that parts of the jet likely started to break off before it struck the ground. The co-pilot, Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, told air traffic controllers minutes before the crash that ice was accumulating on the plane and that severe turbulence had thrown it up and down by more than 700 feet.“We’re going to die!” she said with a scream before the jet slammed into the ground and erupted in a fireball.Family and friends of one of the pilots have been posting online about the longtime aviator, husband and father from the Philadelphia suburbs.Jeff Gregory, 55, was one of two crew members in the cockpit of the Bahamas-bound Learjet 60 as it encountered bad weather and slammed into the ground Sunday afternoon in Greenacres, about 7 miles southwest of West Palm Beach.As the plane plunged, a man’s voice could be heard reciting the Lord’s Prayer in the background of the copilot’s final radio transmissions to air traffic control. Friends are convinced it was Gregory, a devout Christian.Thomas Noetzel, the director of operations at the company that operated the flight, Upper Jets, organized an online fundraiser to support Gregory’s wife and children.Gregory was a close, personal friend and “knowing him has made me a better person,” Noetzel wrote on the fundraising website GoFundMe.“Jeff was a devoted, conscientious, and deeply faithful man who had a genuine passion for flying and a strong love for the Lord ,” Noetzel’s father, Walter, posted on Facebook. “His journey on earth may have ended, but I like to think he is now flying among the angels, soaring peacefully in the presence of our Lord.”Gregory held airline transport pilot and flight instructor certificates, according to Federal Aviation Administration records. He lived in Gilbertsville, about 35 miles (56 kilometers) northwest of Philadelphia, and had previously worked for a charter company based in Allentown, Pennsylvania.“We are deeply saddened to learn that Captain Jeff Gregory was among those who lost their lives,” said April Honnen, the director of charter sales for East Coast Jets, Inc., where he worked in 2016 and 2017. “Our prayers go out to Jeff’s family, his fellow crew member, the passengers and everyone affected by this heart breaking tragedy.”The Learjet hit the ground with enough force to create a crater before bursting into flames. The impact scattered plane fragments over a large area.Images of the moment just before the aircraft made impact appear to show the elevator — a horizontal stabilizer — missing from the tail. About 600 nearby residents remain displaced, but only one injury was reported on the ground.The plane took off from Austin, Texas. The victims included technology entrepreneur Adam Robinson, his wife, Helen Sharp, and their two young children, relatives said.Filgueiras' stepfather, Thiago Corteleti, told the New York Post that she texted her boyfriend about 10 minutes before the crash, telling him: “I’ve got turbulence, I’ve got ice.”The texts were sent before the situation became critical. In the last two minutes of the flight, Filgueiras shifted from calmly communicating with air traffic controllers to calling out terrifying updates as the plane plummeted.The FAA prohibits commercial airline pilots from using cellphones at any point during a flight. The rules aren’t as strict for pilots of charter flights; they are not supposed to use cellphones during critical phases of flight, such as takeoffs and landings, but are allowed while cruising at altitude unless their company or pilot in command specifically bans it.Tom Chapman, a National Transportation Safety Board member, said Monday that weather would be a key focus of the investigation. A preliminary report describing what happened will be released in about a month, but it will likely take more than a year to determine the cause of the crash.

entry.title: Riviera Beach officials warn of long recovery after 1-in-1,000-year flood devastates neighborhoods
entry.summary: Riviera Beach officials gave an update Tuesday afternoon regarding severe flooding, the limits of the city's emergency response, road closures and recovery support as crews worked to reach neighborhoods left devastated by what officials called an approximately 1-in-1,000-year rainfall event. 'Residents needing evacuation assistance are urged to contact the Emergency Operations Center before then and not to wait, as flooding may worsen,' Lawson said. Officials cited about 15.5 inches of rain, with roughly 15 to 20 inches falling within six hours. Flooding has affected Lone Pine Estates , Turtle Cave, 1000 Oaks, Indian Trace and Woodbot, with Lone Pine described as especially devastated. The city has activated its Emergency Operations Center to Level 2 in response to the heavy rain and street flooding across western Riviera Beach. City departments and emergency crews are coordinating closely to protect residents and restore safe conditions as quickly as possible.
