And against big money and long odds, we took our power back."IN CASE YOU MISSED IT | Trump deflects blame for Republican midterm losses as finger-pointing beginsInvestors reacted quickly. SpaceX shares closed down 3.8% on Wednesday and Tesla fell 3.3%, even as the broader market rose, and are tracking even further drops during market trading Thursday.Musk responded on X with a nod to one of his newer ventures: "Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now."Hinojosa inherits the office that oversaw more than $1.6 billion in tax incentives for Musk's companies. She campaigned against generous corporate subsidies and has promised to freeze new data center approvals until the Legislature puts protections in place.Her campaign has said Terafab alone received about $1.7 billion in school tax exemptions. The governor's office also controls the Texas Enterprise Fund, which gave SpaceX $30 million for the project. Tesla is separately seeking state incentives for a proposed $10 billion solar cell plant near Houston.Those incentives matter beyond Musk's balance sheet. When a state grants a company a tax break, that's revenue it doesn't collect, and the cost is typically absorbed by other taxpayers or reflected in public budgets.Hinojosa's win doesn't cancel existing agreements or stop Musk's companies from operating in Texas. But her administration could take a tougher approach to permitting and new incentives as his companies look to expand.Musk also faces a new landscape in Washington, where Democrats will control both the House and Senate in January. Even with President Donald Trump holding veto power, congressional Democrats can issue subpoenas without his signature.

entry.title: Guns, drugs and lots of money: 40 arrested in major Fort Pierce gang takedown - WPBF
entry.summary: Guns, drugs and lots of money: 40 arrested in major Fort Pierce gang takedown    WPBF
entry.article_text: Law enforcement officials in St. Lucie County announced Thursday that 40 suspected members of a Fort Pierce gang have been arrested following an 18-month investigation. The investigation, known as "Operation Score Board," targeted the 23rd Street Gang, which authorities say has operated in northern St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said the gang has between 70 and 80 members and has been responsible for years of violence in the Fort Pierce community. "This gang has terrorized, basically created a hostage crisis for our community up there," Del Toro said. "There’s a lot of good people that are up there in Fort Pierce that have been just held hostage by this group for the last decade, living in fear." Investigators said the gang even maintained a scoreboard tracking shootings and homicides, a discovery that ultimately gave the operation its name. Fort Pierce Police Chief David Smith said detectives reviewed a decade of criminal activity to identify connections between suspected gang members and violent crimes. "Detectives conducted an extensive review of criminal activity spanning ten years, examining incidents and identifying connections between individuals associated with the gang," Smith said. "This intensive analysis revealed a disturbing pattern of organized crime and violence." Authorities said investigators used Florida’s RICO law to connect years of alleged shootings, drug trafficking and other criminal activity to members of the 23rd Street Gang. The investigation involved multiple local and state law enforcement agencies working together over 18 months to build cases against suspected members of the organization. On Wednesday, law enforcement officers executed multiple search warrants throughout the Fort Pierce area, resulting in 11 arrests as part of the larger operation. Authorities said officers also seized multiple firearms, drugs and thousands of dollars in cash. Del Toro said the size of the operation and the cooperation between agencies could have a lasting impact on the community. "I’ve never seen an operation this large with this many agencies at the local and federal level," Del Toro said. "I think this is going to have a significant generational impact in this community." Authorities said similar investigations and operations are expected in the future. entry.title: 23rd Street gang investigation leads to nearly 40 arrests in St. Lucie County - WPEC
entry.summary: 23rd Street gang investigation leads to nearly 40 arrests in St. Lucie County    WPEC
entry.article_text: A nearly two-year investigation into the 23rd Street gang has led to nearly 40 arrests and the seizure of guns, drugs and cash, law enforcement officials said Thursday. The multi-agency investigation, called Operation Score Board, focused on alleged gang activity in northwest Fort Pierce and surrounding areas. Officials said investigators linked 13 people to an alleged criminal conspiracy involving fraud, drug trafficking, shootings and homicides. Fort Pierce Police Chief David Smith said investigators reviewed 10 years of criminal activity and connected people associated with the gang to nearly 100 shootings. Investigators also found that gang members allegedly kept a scoreboard tracking shootings and homicides, which inspired the operation’s name. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office said local, state and federal agencies took part in the investigation. The sheriff’s office, F ort Pierce Police Department , ATF , FBI , DEA , Florida Department of Law Enforcement , U.S. Marshals Service and Homeland Security Investigations were among the participating agencies. "Hundreds of shootings over the last decade, violent crime terrorizing the north end of this county, and our community deserves better, and they're getting better because of the hard work of the men and women with the special investigation units that the chief mentioned, and our federal partners here," said Sheriff Richard Del Toro. Officials said about 70 to 80 people are documented as members of the gang. The investigation focused on people police described as shot callers who allegedly directed its activities. Authorities said the 23rd Street gang has been a problem in the Fort Pierce area for decades and was the most violent of several gangs in the city. 4, officers served five search warrants four in Fort Pierce and one in Port St. Lucie beginning around 5 a.m. The operation led to 11 arrests on racketeering charges, with two people still wanted on warrants, and four additional probable-cause arrests, officials said. Authorities said some people connected to the investigation had already been arrested during its earlier stages. 4 searches yielded seven firearms, about one pound of marijuana, 15 grams of cocaine, 50 grams of MDMA and $18,474. Across the investigation, police said they seized 18 firearms, 20 pounds of marijuana, 532 grams of cocaine and two grams of MDPV. "We remain committed to identifying, investigating, and holding accountable those responsible for bringing violence and criminal activity into our neighborhoods," Chief Smith said. "Our message is clear: We will not tolerate organized criminal activity that threatens the safety of our residents." Authorities did not identify the people they believe led the gang, but said they believe they have arrested most of the key players. They said some people connected to the investigation have faced murder charges, but declined to discuss active cases. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro called the operation an unusually large collaboration among local, state and federal agencies. He said investigators took significant players off the streets and that more operations are expected. The sheriff said the case took extensive work to connect years of records and evidence, and involved a 2,000-page report and a 150-page affidavit. Officials also credited the State Attorney’s Office with helping build the case. History of problems CBS12 previously reported on gang violence in the region, including a 2022 ride-along with St. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office gang intelligence unit Detective Solomon Archie. Archie said Fort Pierce’s 23rd Street and 29th Street gangs operated on opposite sides of the area divided by 25th Street and Martin Luther King Jr. He also described gun violence as a major concern and said law enforcement agencies were working across county lines to identify suspects and respond to crime. In 2017, CBS12 also reported that the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office had launched a six-month crackdown on gangs and drugs in Fort Pierce. At that time, the sheriff said investigators focused on two violent gangs in Fort Pierce, the 10th Street gang and the 23rd Street gang. That operation resulted in more than five dozen arrests and 50 guns seized.

entry.title: William T. Dwyer looks to secure their second straight golf championship
entry.summary: Two years ago, when William T. Dwyer hired Head Golf Coach Eric Fasone, his goal was simple. Our vision was to create a strong program here at Dwyer for boys golf, said Fasone. In year one, the fellas went undefeated and won state, and this year, We went through our regular season with only one loss, and we swept our tournaments, said Fasone. This year, their star is the stellar senior TK Ritthisorn. It wasnt really nerves we knew we were good you know we know our players and we just went out there and did our best and dominated other teams, said Ritthisorn, who was named the district's most outstanding player. It was pretty hard; I played my game and flighted shots and knew what I was doing and I just dominated and played my best, said Ritthisorn. While hes the only returner from last year's championship squad, hes not the only star on the team; in fact theyre team captain is Drew Politziner, who spent the entire season daring his guys to be great. I was very honored that coach gave me the option to be the captain this year for the team and the leadership I give is really overal what Dwyer stands for, said Politziner. With his leadership, TKs clutch skills, and some new faces like Cole Mitchell and Drew Kiernan, the boys swept through districts, sectionals, and regionals. Going into districts I knew we were supposed to win it again and regionals I didnt really know much about the course, said Mitchell. We got the Mamba Mentality, so were supposed to go out and win every single match and do the best we can, said Kiernan. That Mamba mentality has the fellas headed to the state Tournament this weekend, a moment the guys have been waiting on. Im excited to see what everyone can do and play their best, and no matter how hard it is, everyone will do their part,' said junior Tyler Sheehan.

entry.title: 'It's still rising': Jensen Beach homes flooded - WPTV
entry.summary: 'It's still rising': Jensen Beach homes flooded    WPTV
entry.article_text: Much of a Jensen Beach neighborhood on Hyline Drive is underwater after this week's heavy rain overwhelmed the local drainage system. As of Wednesday afternoon, water levels inside some homes are still rising long after the rain stopped.For Lisa French and Tiffany Kincaid, a kayak has become the way to get around their flooded community.WATCH REPORT BELOW: At Kincaid's home, the water level is waist-deep."We're currently taking stuff out of our house right now, salvaging what we can," said Kincaid.At French's home, the damage has just begun, with the water level climbing to 4 inches deep."My floorboards are outside, but it's still rising. My husband made a mark inside so it's still coming up and ours isn't nearly as bad as everyone else," French said.Their homes are among dozens in the neighborhood under water after Monday's heavy rain saturated the ground and inundated the drainage system."We were expecting flooding to go down. Clearly drainage is not — things are not draining correctly," Kincaid said.Martin County told us the neighborhood is uniquely located next to the Savannas Preserve, where water is naturally flowing south from other areas that flooded. For now, the county says it's unable to pump water out of the community because the nearby watershed doesn't have capacity, but relief may be on the horizon."As the water level drops, that's going to drain the ponds that we need to pump into, and that's going to allow us to do that," Martin County's Public Works Director Jim Gordon said. "We're maximizing what we can downstream, and we might see it trending in the right direction."Residents are hoping relief comes sooner rather than later so they can start the long road to recovery."Even after, like, our houses are wrecked," French said."It's just a lot to take in right now for us," Kincaid said.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. Our editorial team verifies all reporting on all platforms for fairness and accuracy.

According to the Vero Beach Police Department , the incident happened around 12:59 a.m. 1 at the hotel, located at 3101 Ocean Drive. Investigators said surveillance footage captured four individuals at the property. Witnesses reported hearing loud banging or kicking noises before discovering damage to a room's door and door frame. Polie released surveillance images of the individuals as part of an effort to identify them. The department classified the incident as criminal mischief. See also: Resources for residents and business owners after heavy rain and flooding Anyone who recognizes the individuals or has information about the incident is asked to contact Detective Fonseca with the Vero Beach Police Department at 772-978-4667 or by email at gfonseca@vbpd.org. People wishing to remain anonymous can contact Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 800-273-8477. Tipsters may be eligible for a cash reward. The investigation remains ongoing.

Nearly 100 residents were trapped in stranded vehicles as floodwaters rapidly rose.WATCH BELOW: Flooding in Century VillageFirefighters reported encountering floating cars with people still inside and water reaching between 3 and 4 feet deep in some areas.Crews deployed drones equipped with thermal imaging cameras around Century Village, Cypress Lakes, the Tennis Club and other areas to search vehicles for people who needed help.Firefighters then waded through the water and used high-water vehicles and brush trucks to rescue residents and bring them to higher ground.Fire Rescue said there were no injuries during those operations.Palm Beach County Fire Rescue's Urban Search and Rescue Swiftwater Response Team was also deployed to Riviera Beach for nearly 24 hours.With some streets impassable, rescue specialists used emergency rafts and boats to go door to door.Fire Rescue said its teams:Evacuated 71 peopleConducted two medical rescuesEvacuated nine petsCounty officials have continued reporting significant impacts from the flooding in Riviera Beach and other communities.PBCFR said from Nov. 1-3, crews responded to a total of more than 1,600 emergency calls across the county. entry.title: NTSB recovers part of Learjet engine, asks public to report crash debris
entry.summary: Investigators have recovered a portion of an engine from the Learjet 60 that crashed near Greenacres on Sunday as crews continue excavating the crash site, according to the National Transportation Safety Board. The NTSB said excavation work began late Wednesday and continued Thursday as investigators and local officials worked to recover wreckage from the crash that killed nine people. WATCH BELOW: Piece of jet's tail found miles away NTSB: Piece of Learjet's tail found miles away from crash Debris from the aircraft has been found away from the main impact site, including on the roofs of nearby homes and buildings, according to the NTSB. All recovered wreckage will be taken to a secure location for further examination. Investigators are also asking residents who find debris believed to be from the Learjet not to keep it or attempt to move, alter or dispose of it. The agency said even small pieces of wreckage could contain evidence that helps investigators determine what happened. Anyone who has found or collected debris from the crash is asked to email witness@ntsb.gov to arrange for its recovery. The NTSB is asking people to include a photograph of the debris in the email, if possible. The NTSB said recovering as much of the aircraft wreckage as possible is critical to its investigation and efforts to determine the cause of the crash.

entry.title: GOP meltdown sparks battle over who's to blame
entry.summary: Even as key Senate races remain unresolved in Mississippi and Alaska, Republicans have already begun searching for someone to blame after a devastating midterm election defeat. With Democrats securing control of the Senate and on track for major gains in the House, the conversation in Washington has quickly shifted from counting ballots to assigning responsibility. The outstanding races remain extraordinarily close. In Mississippi, just over 1,000 votes separate the candidates, with additional mail ballots still eligible to arrive under state law. Alaska's contest may take even longer to resolve because of its ranked-choice voting system, where second- and third-choice preferences could ultimately determine the winner. But while election officials continue tallying votes, Republicans are increasingly focused on what many in the party view as one of the worst electoral setbacks in decades. RELATED STORY | Democratic leaders outline agenda after sweeping Congress in midterms The finger-pointing has already begun. One of the first casualties appears to be House Republican leadership. Speaker Mike Johnson has announced he will not seek another term as the party's leader in the House, guaranteeing a new face at the helm as Republicans attempt to regroup. Attention is also turning toward the White House and Trump's inner circle. Vice President JD Vance sparked discussion across Washington after publicly arguing that the party's losses were primarily tied to the conflict with Iran. WATCH: Pete Hegseth's future hangs in the balance Trump puts new scrutiny on Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth In a social media post, Vance argued that the war was the central reason for the GOP's defeat and suggested any effort to rebuild the party must begin with an honest assessment of that decision. The comments have intensified scrutiny on senior administration officials, particularly Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Some Republicans are openly questioning whether changes at the Pentagon or elsewhere in the administration are necessary after the election results. The debate echoes a familiar chapter in modern political history. Following Republican losses in the 2006 midterm elections, President George W. Bush replaced Defense Secretary Donald Rumsfeld amid growing criticism over the Iraq War. Some Republicans are drawing parallels between that election and the party's current predicament. RELATED STORY | DNC chair says Democrats must deliver on promises after midterm wins President

entry.title: William T. Dwyer looks to secure their second straight golf championship
entry.summary: Two years ago, when William T. Dwyer hired head golf coach Eric Fasone, his goal was simple. 'Our vision was to create a strong program here at Dwyer for boys' golf,' said Fasone. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Dwyer seeks 2nd straight golf championship In year one, the fellas went undefeated and won state, and this year, 'We went through our regular season with only one loss, and we swept our tournaments,' said Fasone. This year, their star is the stellar senior TK Ritthisorn. 'It wasnt really nerves; we knew we were good, you know, we know our players, and we just went out there and did our best and dominated other teams,' said Ritthisorn, who was named the district's most outstanding player. 'It was pretty hard; I played my game and flighted shots and knew what I was doing, and I just dominated and played my best,' said Ritthisorn. While hes the only returner from last year's championship squad, he's not the only star on the team; in fact theyre team captain is Drew Politziner, who spent the entire season daring his guys to be great. 'I was very honored that coach gave me the option to be the captain this year for the team, and the leadership I give is really overall what Dwyer stands for,' said Politziner. With his leadership, TKs clutch skills, and some new faces like Cole Mitchell and Drew Kiernan, the boys swept through districts, sectionals, and regionals. 'Going into districts, I knew we were supposed to win it again, and regionals I didnt really know much about the course,' said Mitchell. 'We got the Mamba Mentality, so were supposed to go out and win every single match and do the best we can,' said Kiernan. That Mamba mentality has the fellas headed to the state Tournament this weekend, a moment the guys have been waiting on. 'Im excited to see what everyone can do and play their best, and no matter how hard it is, everyone will do their part,' said junior Tyler Sheehan.

entry.title: Martin County flooding leaves cattle farmers struggling, residents demanding solutions - WPBF
entry.summary: Martin County flooding leaves cattle farmers struggling, residents demanding solutions    WPBF
entry.article_text: Floodwaters continue to inundate properties in Martin County, leaving cattle farmers struggling to care for their animals and residents concerned about how much longer the water will remain. Residents in the Trailside community say water from neighboring properties is flowing into their drainage system, causing widespread flooding. Flooding threatens cattle, farm operations Hungryland Farms normally operates a 20-acre rotational grazing system for its Florida Cracker cattle. The owner, Melissa, said much of the pasture is now underwater, forcing the animals onto the farm’s elevated driveway. "We're starting to lose big sections of the driveway. We have them concentrated up the house pad, but if we lose too much more, we're just going to have to figure out a way to evacuate them somewhere," she said. Some cattle have struggled to navigate the water, and Melissa said the farm is concerned about losing access to its property as flooding continues. For now, the farm is bringing in hay and hay cubes to keep the cattle on their regular diet while monitoring potential health risks from floodwaters. "We’re more just concerned with the health and safety of our cattle," Melissa said. Melissa said the farm has an emergency contact with the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Natural Resources Conservation Service if the animals face imminent danger. "We don’t know how long we’re going to be here," she said. HOA says solution is unclear Kyla Shay, president of the Trailside Homeowners Association, said the community’s drainage system is designed to handle water from its 41 lots and designated neighboring properties. However, Shay said water from outside that system is now flowing through county-owned land and other neighboring properties before reaching the community’s southern canal. We can’t handle theirs," Shay said. The flooding has also affected neighboring pastures and reached areas near Bridge Road and an electrical substation, according to Shay. She said some electrical transformers are partially underwater, septic systems are overwhelmed and residents have been warned their well water could be compromised. "The health department issued warnings this morning to me that our water wells could be compromised because of bacteria, because of the standing water," Shay said. Since their septic systems are submerged, Shay said homeowners have been unable to shower or do laundry. County says repairs must wait WPBF 25 News reached out to Martin County about their concerns and learned the county recently acquired approximately 315 acres of land in the area, known as the Elise J. A county spokesperson said establishing access has been their immediate priority so staff can assess conditions and respond. The county said it is working with the Hobe-St. Lucie Conservancy District to address a breach affecting drainage into its irrigation canal and that the agencies jointly determined repairs should wait until water levels recede. The county said current conditions make hauling and placing sand unsafe and potentially damaging to the levee. Material could also wash into the canal before crews establish a stable repair. "County staff will continue to monitor water levels and site conditions in close coordination with the Hobe-St. Lucie Conservancy District," a county spokesperson said. The county said it will move forward with repairs when conditions allow safe work without compromising the levee. It is also evaluating longer-term options to improve outflow and reduce the risk of flooding happening again. Residents want a long-term solution Shay said the homeowners association has been working with water engineers and other experts to understand how long the flooding could last. "It's probably going to be late January, February before we can see a break, and that's assuming that the south canal wall does not collapse and immediately dump all the water on us," she said. Melissa said the farm’s drainage system normally provides room for water to collect during the rainy season, but the amount coming from outside the property has overwhelmed it. "We have a very extensive drainage system, but it’s just not equipped to handle this amount of water," Melissa said. Both women said they want neighboring properties and the agencies responsible for drainage to address the problem. For now, Martin County said it will continue monitoring conditions and coordinating with the conservancy district before attempting repairs. Meanwhile, Melissa said the farm is focused on keeping its cattle safe as water continues to surround the property.

entry.article_text: Lucie County flipped blue in Tuesday's governor's race for the first time in more than a decade, as voter turnout climbed despite historic flooding that forced last-minute polling place changes. Democrat David Jolly carried the county with approximately 51% of the vote , compared with 48% for Republican Byron Donalds. The result marked the first time since 2012 that a Democratic candidate for governor or president won a majority in St. That year, former President Barack Obama carried the county with 53.42% of the vote. According to TCPalm , voter turnout reached 56.5% in the county, up 5.2 percentage points from the 2022 general election , when 51.3% of registered voters cast ballots. Lucie County ranked 51st among Florida's 67 counties, with only 16 counties reporting lower turnout. In 2022, the county had 238,645 registered voters, with 122,361 casting ballots. See also: Neighborhoods in Jensen Beach go underwater as flooding devastates the Treasure Coast Voters turn out despite historic flooding The increase came as widespread flooding forced election officials to relocate several polling places across Port St. Lucie, Tradition and Fort Pierce, per CBS12 reports . Lucie County Supervisor of Elections Gertrude Walker said the changes were necessary to ensure voters had safe and accessible locations to cast their ballots. Voters assigned to Oak Hammock K-8 School, Centennial High School and the Paula A. Lewis Library were among those affected, with some redirected to the Port St. Lucie Community Center, Indian River State College's Veterans Center of Excellence and Tradition Town Hall. The changes followed heavy rainfall that submerged roads, stranded vehicles and prompted evacuations across parts of the county. Ron DeSantis declared a state of emergency for St. Lucie County and six other Florida counties, while flooding forced local public schools to close Tuesday and Wednesday. Despite the weather-related challenges, St. Lucie County surpassed its 2022 general election turnout rate while delivering a Democratic majority in the governor's race for the first time in 14 years, when Obama won the county. While the flooding complicated Election Day logistics, the higher turnout suggests those challenges did not prevent overall participation from exceeding the previous gubernatorial election.

entry.summary: Friends of 18-year-old Kenneth Kenny Donahue are mourning the Spanish River High School senior after he was killed in an e-bike crash on West Palmetto Park Road in Boca Raton, just hours after spending Halloween night with friends. Donahue's friends told WPTV reporter Zitlali Solache they are struggling with the sudden loss while remembering the plans they had made together, including attending college. Thats where it happened, so it deserves to be known, said Sawyer Geldert, a close friend of Kenny. The memorial is a place for Donahue's loved ones to remember the 18-year-old they describe as funny, loving, optimistic and caring. I still text him, Geldert said. It hurts to lose someone so close to you. And if I could see him one last time, I would hug him and never let go. Police investigating crash on West Palmetto Park Road The Boca Raton Police Services Department said its Traffic Homicide Unit is investigating the crash, which happened shortly before 2 a.m. on West Palmetto Park Road between Interstate 95 and Military Trail. According to police, the driver of a 2025 blue Corvette was traveling east on West Palmetto Park Road when the car struck an electric bicycle carrying two people. Police said Donahue was the passenger on the e-bike and suffered fatal injuries. He was pronounced dead at the scene. Police said the 16-year-old operating the e-bike was taken to a hospital and was listed in stable condition. The Corvette driver was not injured. entry.title: 'It's still rising': Jensen Beach homes flooded - WPTV
entry.summary: 'It's still rising': Jensen Beach homes flooded    WPTV
entry.article_text: Much of a Jensen Beach neighborhood on Hyline Drive is underwater after this week's heavy rain overwhelmed the local drainage system. As of Wednesday afternoon, water levels inside some homes are still rising long after the rain stopped.For Lisa French and Tiffany Kincaid, a kayak has become the way to get around their flooded community.WATCH REPORT BELOW: At Kincaid's home, the water level is waist-deep."We're currently taking stuff out of our house right now, salvaging what we can," said Kincaid.At French's home, the damage has just begun, with the water level climbing to 4 inches deep."My floorboards are outside, but it's still rising. My husband made a mark inside so it's still coming up and ours isn't nearly as bad as everyone else," French said.Their homes are among dozens in the neighborhood under water after Monday's heavy rain saturated the ground and inundated the drainage system."We were expecting flooding to go down. Clearly drainage is not — things are not draining correctly," Kincaid said.Martin County told us the neighborhood is uniquely located next to the Savannas Preserve, where water is naturally flowing south from other areas that flooded. For now, the county says it's unable to pump water out of the community because the nearby watershed doesn't have capacity, but relief may be on the horizon."As the water level drops, that's going to drain the ponds that we need to pump into, and that's going to allow us to do that," Martin County's Public Works Director Jim Gordon said. "We're maximizing what we can downstream, and we might see it trending in the right direction."Residents are hoping relief comes sooner rather than later so they can start the long road to recovery."Even after, like, our houses are wrecked," French said."It's just a lot to take in right now for us," Kincaid said.This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. entry.title: 23rd Street gang investigation leads to nearly 40 arrests in St. Lucie County - cw34.com
entry.summary: 23rd Street gang investigation leads to nearly 40 arrests in St. Lucie County    cw34.com
entry.article_text: A nearly two-year investigation into the 23rd Street gang has led to nearly 40 arrests and the seizure of guns, drugs and cash, law enforcement officials said Thursday. The multi-agency investigation, called Operation Score Board, focused on alleged gang activity in northwest Fort Pierce and surrounding areas. Officials said investigators linked 13 people to an alleged criminal conspiracy involving fraud, drug trafficking, shootings and homicides. Fort Pierce Police Chief David Smith said investigators reviewed 10 years of criminal activity and connected people associated with the gang to nearly 100 shootings. Investigators also found that gang members allegedly kept a scoreboard tracking shootings and homicides, which inspired the operation’s name. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office said local, state and federal agencies took part in the investigation. The sheriff’s office, F ort Pierce Police Department , ATF , FBI , DEA , Florida Department of Law Enforcement , U.S. Marshals Service and Homeland Security Investigations were among the participating agencies. "Hundreds of shootings over the last decade, violent crime terrorizing the north end of this county, and our community deserves better, and they're getting better because of the hard work of the men and women with the special investigation units that the chief mentioned, and our federal partners here," said Sheriff Richard Del Toro. Officials said about 70 to 80 people are documented as members of the gang. The investigation focused on people police described as shot callers who allegedly directed its activities. Authorities said the 23rd Street gang has been a problem in the Fort Pierce area for decades and was the most violent of several gangs in the city. 4, officers served five search warrants four in Fort Pierce and one in Port St. Lucie beginning around 5 a.m. The operation led to 11 arrests on racketeering charges, with two people still wanted on warrants, and four additional probable-cause arrests, officials said. Authorities said some people connected to the investigation had already been arrested during its earlier stages. 4 searches yielded seven firearms, about one pound of marijuana, 15 grams of cocaine, 50 grams of MDMA and $18,474. Across the investigation, police said they seized 18 firearms, 20 pounds of marijuana, 532 grams of cocaine and two grams of MDPV. "We remain committed to identifying, investigating, and holding accountable those responsible for bringing violence and criminal activity into our neighborhoods," Chief Smith said. "Our message is clear: We will not tolerate organized criminal activity that threatens the safety of our residents." Authorities did not identify the people they believe led the gang, but said they believe they have arrested most of the key players. They said some people connected to the investigation have faced murder charges, but declined to discuss active cases. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro called the operation an unusually large collaboration among local, state and federal agencies. He said investigators took significant players off the streets and that more operations are expected. The sheriff said the case took extensive work to connect years of records and evidence, and involved a 2,000-page report and a 150-page affidavit. Officials also credited the State Attorney’s Office with helping build the case. History of problems CBS12 previously reported on gang violence in the region, including a 2022 ride-along with St. Lucie County Sheriff’s Office gang intelligence unit Detective Solomon Archie. Archie said Fort Pierce’s 23rd Street and 29th Street gangs operated on opposite sides of the area divided by 25th Street and Martin Luther King Jr. He also described gun violence as a major concern and said law enforcement agencies were working across county lines to identify suspects and respond to crime. In 2017, CBS12 also reported that the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office had launched a six-month crackdown on gangs and drugs in Fort Pierce. At that time, the sheriff said investigators focused on two violent gangs in Fort Pierce, the 10th Street gang and the 23rd Street gang. That operation resulted in more than five dozen arrests and 50 guns seized.

entry.title: Port St. Lucie grandmother grateful after flood rescue from van swept into canal - WPEC
entry.summary: Port St. Lucie grandmother grateful after flood rescue from van swept into canal    WPEC
entry.article_text: Maria Andrade-Vasquez of Port St. Lucie has overcome plenty of challenges in her life. The mother of four, grandmother of 10, cancer survivor and dialysis patient never imagined a routine ride home from treatment would turn into a fight for survival. On Monday, Andrade-Vasquez was riding home from dialysis when floodwaters swept the transport van she was in off the road near Lakehurst Drive and into a canal in Port St. Lucie's Swan Park community. Speaking with CBS12 News through her son, Raul Morales, who translated from Spanish, Andrade-Vasquez said she feared she would not survive. "Yes, very, very scared," she said. Morales said as floodwaters rose around the van, his mother thought she might be living her final moments. Also see: Officer, firefighters rescue two from vehicle swept into Port St. Lucie canal "Seeing all the water go up, she was thinking, what's going to happen? Is this it?" Morales said. Police body camera video released this week shows how quickly first responders reacted. Lucie police said Officer Peterson arrived just 100 seconds after being dispatched to reports of a transport van that had gone into a canal off Southwest Hogan Street. Video captured the officer rushing into the water and rescuing the driver first before learning another passenger was still trapped inside. That passenger was Andrade-Vasquez. As water surrounded the vehicle, rescuers say the van tilted into the canal, leaving her trapped in the back. Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said the same wheelchair equipment used to help Andrade-Vasquez after dialysis treatments was now blocking her escape. "She's wheelchair bound, so the equipment that came out of the back of the van was up in place blocking her in," Niemczyk said. "They had to get her out of the wheelchair and pull her up over the equipment to get her out of the van." According to police, firefighters with St. Lucie County Fire District joined the officer at the scene and worked together to free Andrade-Vasquez from the vehicle. Morales said his mother still struggles to understand how rescuers were able to get her out so quickly. "She said, 'I don't know how they did it, but they quickly released her,'" Morales said. "To me it was amazing to see how quick they did what they did." Both Andrade-Vasquez and the driver were rescued safely. Her rescue was one of dozens of flood-related emergencies first responders handled as rainfall inundated roads and neighborhoods across Port St. Now recovering at home with her family, Andrade-Vasquez remains grateful to the first responders who helped save her life. The way I see it, you guys went the extra mile," Morales said. So thank you." Morales said his mother is still processing the trauma of the rescue but plans to continue her dialysis treatments three times a week as she focuses on her recovery.

entry.title: Viral video of student swimming home raises safety concerns in Port St. Lucie - WPBF
entry.summary: Viral video of student swimming home raises safety concerns in Port St. Lucie    WPBF
entry.article_text: A viral video showing a student swimming home from a school bus in flooded Port St. Lucie streets has raised questions about why schools opened during Monday’s severe weather. The video, filmed in a neighborhood where water has since receded, shows the student navigating deep floodwaters after exiting the bus. "He literally almost went completely underwater," said Lucinda Lopez, a Port St. Another neighbor, Ariel Abel, described the scene: "We watched the school bus get stuck over in that turn area, and then we watched the kid get off, and he sunk straight into the water." The incident has left parents questioning why schools opened on Monday despite the flooding. Concerns include why buses were sent into severely flooded streets and whether students should have sheltered in place at school until conditions improved. "Seeing the danger that all of the kids were put in is not okay," Lopez said. Abel added, "They really dropped the ball on this. The community is disappointed." On Tuesday, St. Lucie Public Schools Superintendent Dr. Jon Prince addressed the situation during a news conference, apologizing to families for the district’s response. The first flood advisory for the county came in just after 8 a.m. Monday, with the first flash flood warning issued at 10:41 a.m. "I completely understand the frustration families feel," Prince said. "It caused a lot of stress for our families, and for that, I’m profoundly sorry." Despite the apology, some parents remain unsatisfied. "An apology doesn’t fix what is happening," Abel said. Lopez emphasized the need for change: "We need to do better. We need to protect our kids at all costs. Missing a day or two of school is okay if it means keeping our kids safe at all costs." WPBF is working to hear from the school district to address these concerns and questions. entry.summary: Martin County flooding leaves cattle farmers struggling, residents demanding solutions    WPBF
entry.article_text: Floodwaters continue to inundate properties in Martin County, leaving cattle farmers struggling to care for their animals and residents concerned about how much longer the water will remain. Residents in the Trailside community say water from neighboring properties is flowing into their drainage system, causing widespread flooding. Flooding threatens cattle, farm operations Hungryland Farms normally operates a 20-acre rotational grazing system for its Florida Cracker cattle. The owner, Melissa, said much of the pasture is now underwater, forcing the animals onto the farm’s elevated driveway. "We're starting to lose big sections of the driveway. We have them concentrated up the house pad, but if we lose too much more, we're just going to have to figure out a way to evacuate them somewhere," she said. Some cattle have struggled to navigate the water, and Melissa said the farm is concerned about losing access to its property as flooding continues. For now, the farm is bringing in hay and hay cubes to keep the cattle on their regular diet while monitoring potential health risks from floodwaters. "We’re more just concerned with the health and safety of our cattle," Melissa said. Melissa said the farm has an emergency contact with the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Natural Resources Conservation Service if the animals face imminent danger. "We don’t know how long we’re going to be here," she said. HOA says solution is unclear Kyla Shay, president of the Trailside Homeowners Association, said the community’s drainage system is designed to handle water from its 41 lots and designated neighboring properties. However, Shay said water from outside that system is now flowing through county-owned land and other neighboring properties before reaching the community’s southern canal. We can’t handle theirs," Shay said. The flooding has also affected neighboring pastures and reached areas near Bridge Road and an electrical substation, according to Shay. She said some electrical transformers are partially underwater, septic systems are overwhelmed and residents have been warned their well water could be compromised. "The health department issued warnings this morning to me that our water wells could be compromised because of bacteria, because of the standing water," Shay said. Since their septic systems are submerged, Shay said homeowners have been unable to shower or do laundry. County says repairs must wait WPBF 25 News reached out to Martin County about their concerns and learned the county recently acquired approximately 315 acres of land in the area, known as the Elise J. A county spokesperson said establishing access has been their immediate priority so staff can assess conditions and respond. The county said it is working with the Hobe-St. Lucie Conservancy District to address a breach affecting drainage into its irrigation canal and that the agencies jointly determined repairs should wait until water levels recede. The county said current conditions make hauling and placing sand unsafe and potentially damaging to the levee. Material could also wash into the canal before crews establish a stable repair. "County staff will continue to monitor water levels and site conditions in close coordination with the Hobe-St. Lucie Conservancy District," a county spokesperson said. The county said it will move forward with repairs when conditions allow safe work without compromising the levee. It is also evaluating longer-term options to improve outflow and reduce the risk of flooding happening again. Residents want a long-term solution Shay said the homeowners association has been working with water engineers and other experts to understand how long the flooding could last. "It's probably going to be late January, February before we can see a break, and that's assuming that the south canal wall does not collapse and immediately dump all the water on us," she said. Melissa said the farm’s drainage system normally provides room for water to collect during the rainy season, but the amount coming from outside the property has overwhelmed it. "We have a very extensive drainage system, but it’s just not equipped to handle this amount of water," Melissa said. Both women said they want neighboring properties and the agencies responsible for drainage to address the problem. For now, Martin County said it will continue monitoring conditions and coordinating with the conservancy district before attempting repairs. Meanwhile, Melissa said the farm is focused on keeping its cattle safe as water continues to surround the property.

entry.title: Guns, drugs and lots of money: 40 arrested in major Fort Pierce gang takedown - WPBF
entry.summary: Guns, drugs and lots of money: 40 arrested in major Fort Pierce gang takedown    WPBF
entry.article_text: Law enforcement officials in St. Lucie County announced Thursday that 40 suspected members of a Fort Pierce gang have been arrested following an 18-month investigation. The investigation, known as "Operation Score Board," targeted the 23rd Street Gang, which authorities say has operated in northern St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said the gang has between 70 and 80 members and has been responsible for years of violence in the Fort Pierce community. "This gang has terrorized, basically created a hostage crisis for our community up there," Del Toro said. "There’s a lot of good people that are up there in Fort Pierce that have been just held hostage by this group for the last decade, living in fear." Investigators said the gang even maintained a scoreboard tracking shootings and homicides, a discovery that ultimately gave the operation its name. Fort Pierce Police Chief David Smith said detectives reviewed a decade of criminal activity to identify connections between suspected gang members and violent crimes. "Detectives conducted an extensive review of criminal activity spanning ten years, examining incidents and identifying connections between individuals associated with the gang," Smith said. "This intensive analysis revealed a disturbing pattern of organized crime and violence." Authorities said investigators used Florida’s RICO law to connect years of alleged shootings, drug trafficking and other criminal activity to members of the 23rd Street Gang. The investigation involved multiple local and state law enforcement agencies working together over 18 months to build cases against suspected members of the organization. On Wednesday, law enforcement officers executed multiple search warrants throughout the Fort Pierce area, resulting in 11 arrests as part of the larger operation. Authorities said officers also seized multiple firearms, drugs and thousands of dollars in cash. Del Toro said the size of the operation and the cooperation between agencies could have a lasting impact on the community. "I’ve never seen an operation this large with this many agencies at the local and federal level," Del Toro said. "I think this is going to have a significant generational impact in this community." Authorities said similar investigations and operations are expected in the future. entry.summary: With Democrats poised to take control of both chambers of Congress, attention is quickly turning from the 2026 midterm elections to the leadership battles that will determine who guides the new House and Senate majorities. Jeffries would be in position to become House speaker, while Schumer would become Senate majority leader. Both, however, have faced calls from some progressive activists and incoming lawmakers for a change in leadership. Critics argue Democratic leaders did not push back aggressively enough against President Donald Trump while the party was in the minority. entry.title: 'I miss him': Friends mourn Boca Raton teen killed in e-bike crash
entry.summary: Friends of 18-year-old Kenneth 'Kenny' Donahue are mourning the Spanish River High School senior after he was killed in an e-bike crash on West Palmetto Park Road in Boca Raton, just hours after spending Halloween night with friends. Donahue's friends told WPTV reporter Zitlali Solache they are struggling with the sudden loss while remembering the plans they had made together, including attending college. Watch report from Zitlali Solache: I still text him: Friends mourn Boca Raton teen killed in e-bike crash A blue cross now marks the area along West Palmetto Park Road where the crash occurred. 'That's where it happened, so it deserves to be known,' said Sawyer Geldert, a close friend of Kenny. entry.title: NTSB recovers part of Learjet engine, asks public to report crash debris
entry.summary: Investigators have recovered a portion of an engine from the Learjet 60 that crashed near Greenacres on Sunday as crews continue excavating the crash site, according to the National Transportation Safety Board. The NTSB said excavation work began late Wednesday and continued Thursday as investigators and local officials worked to recover wreckage from the crash that killed nine people. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Part of jet's engine found, NTSB says NTSB recovers part of Learjet engine after crash Debris from the aircraft has been found away from the main impact site, including on the roofs of nearby homes and buildings, according to the NTSB. All recovered wreckage will be taken to a secure location for further examination. Investigators are also asking residents who find debris believed to be from the Learjet not to keep it or attempt to move, alter or dispose of it. WATCH BELOW: Piece of jet's tail found miles away NTSB: Piece of Learjet's tail found miles away from crash The agency said even small pieces of wreckage could contain evidence that helps investigators determine what happened. Anyone who has found or collected debris from the crash is asked to email witness@ntsb.gov to arrange for its recovery. The NTSB is asking people to include a photograph of the debris in the email, if possible. The NTSB said recovering as much of the aircraft wreckage as possible is critical to its investigation and efforts to determine the cause of the crash.

entry.title: Flooding leaves Creekside community in St. Lucie County without power, most homes evacuated
entry.summary: Floodwaters remain knee-deep in parts of the Creekside community in St. Lucie County, where officials say roughly 75% of the neighborhood's homes have been evacuated, and power remains shut off. St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro provided a Thursday update , saying the community, located off State Road 70 west of Florida's Turnpike, has about 150 homes and remains under a voluntary evacuation. WATCH REPORT BELOW: Flooding leaves Creekside community in St. Lucie County without power, Del Toro said some trucks can now make it into the neighborhood, but water levels remain high. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office also has a high-water vehicle available to assist residents who need help. 'If in fact you need help, please don't hesitate to call 911 or contact one of our deputies,' Del Toro said. Deputies are providing 24-hour security in the community while residents remain displaced and electricity is out, according to the sheriff. WATCH AERIAL VIDEO OF THE FLOODING: Aerial video of flooding in the Creekside community of St. Lucie County Restoring power could take additional time because some of Florida Power Light's equipment remains underwater. 'We continue to monitor the water level just like everybody else,' FPL's Marshall Critchfield said. 'Much of our equipment is presently underwater and our priority number one, as always, is safety.' Critchfield said crews will restore electricity as soon as water recedes enough for them to safely access the equipment. Del Toro said the neighborhood has underground utilities, creating an additional challenge while flooding remains high. Officials did not provide an estimate for when power would be restored or when the water is expected to fully recede. Del Toro urged residents who need assistance to contact deputies or call 911.

entry.title: Father of Meghan Markle arrested on charges related to child sexual abuse material, AP sources say
entry.summary: Meghan Markle's father was arrested Friday morning by federal agents in Florida on charges related to child sexual abuse material, two people familiar with the matter told The Associated Press. Thomas Markle Sr. was arrested outside Tampa, according to the people who were not authorized to publicly discuss the investigation and spoke on the condition of anonymity. His arrest follows reports by The Sun, a British tabloid newspaper, that Meghan's half brother found a collection of child sexual abuse images while clearing out the home of their father in the Philippines. Meghan Markle, the wife of Prince Harry, recently said she was 'deeply distressed' by allegations that a collection of child sexual abuse images had been found at her fathers former home. She also revealed that a letter containing troubling allegations about him had been sent to London police in 2018. 'It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated, Meghan said of the letter. 'I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children was for one reason: to protect them . Meghan, an American citizen who starred in the U.S. television drama Suits, married Harry at Windsor Castle in 2018. They have two children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet. Her father, a retired television lighting and photography director, did not attend the wedding, prompting extensive coverage in the British media of Meghans estrangement from her father. Thomas Markle Sr. was living in the Philippines earlier this year when he suffered a stroke and had his left leg amputated. That forced him to return to the U.S. The Sun reported that Thomas Markle Jr. recently found hundreds, if not thousands of child sex abuse images in boxes at his fathers former home in Cebu City, in the Philippines, when he was clearing out the property. Markle Jr. told the newspaper that he reported the images to police in the Philippines and contacted the FBI. 'I have supported, cared for him and helped him for years but that stops now,' Markle Jr. told The Sun. 'I won't speak to my father ever again unless Im called to give evidence against him.'

entry.title: Viral video of student swimming home raises safety concerns in Port St. Lucie - WPBF
entry.summary: Viral video of student swimming home raises safety concerns in Port St. Lucie    WPBF
entry.article_text: A viral video showing a student swimming home from a school bus in flooded Port St. Lucie streets has raised questions about why schools opened during Monday’s severe weather. The video, filmed in a neighborhood where water has since receded, shows the student navigating deep floodwaters after exiting the bus. "He literally almost went completely underwater," said Lucinda Lopez, a Port St. Another neighbor, Ariel Abel, described the scene: "We watched the school bus get stuck over in that turn area, and then we watched the kid get off, and he sunk straight into the water." The incident has left parents questioning why schools opened on Monday despite the flooding. Concerns include why buses were sent into severely flooded streets and whether students should have sheltered in place at school until conditions improved. "Seeing the danger that all of the kids were put in is not okay," Lopez said. Abel added, "They really dropped the ball on this. The community is disappointed." On Tuesday, St. Lucie Public Schools Superintendent Dr. Jon Prince addressed the situation during a news conference, apologizing to families for the district’s response. The first flood advisory for the county came in just after 8 a.m. Monday, with the first flash flood warning issued at 10:41 a.m. "I completely understand the frustration families feel," Prince said. "It caused a lot of stress for our families, and for that, I’m profoundly sorry." Despite the apology, some parents remain unsatisfied. "An apology doesn’t fix what is happening," Abel said. Lopez emphasized the need for change: "We need to do better. We need to protect our kids at all costs. Missing a day or two of school is okay if it means keeping our kids safe at all costs." WPBF is working to hear from the school district to address these concerns and questions. entry.title: Neighbors hear 'sound of a bomb' in Fort Pierce operation - WPBF
entry.summary: Neighbors hear 'sound of a bomb' in Fort Pierce operation    WPBF
entry.article_text: Residents in a Fort Pierce neighborhood were awakened early Wednesday morning by loud explosions as law enforcement agencies carried out a large-scale operation involving five search warrants across St. Neighbors along Miami Court described the startling events. "When you heard the sound, it sounded like a bomb; I thought, 'That's not a regular handgun, that sounds like a bomb,'" one neighbor said. "There were so many of them they were like a military. There was a military truck out there too," the neighbor added. Law enforcement vehicles were seen investigating at two homes in the area — one at 1708 Miami Court and another nearby at 1904 Georgia Avenue. Lucie County Sheriff's Office confirmed the operation was part of a large-scale criminal investigation, with the Drug Enforcement Administration and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives also present at the scene. That same neighbor shared her experience, saying, "I heard what sounded like bombs going off. Boom, and I said, 'What the heck is going on?' I peeked out the door, and I saw the blue lights from the police." She said the noises woke her up, and she watched as officers blocked off the road and issued commands over a loudspeaker. Authorities have not released details about the investigation or what led to the arrests, but the sheriff's office stated there is no known threat to the community.

entry.title: Father of Meghan Markle arrested on charges related to child sexual abuse material in Florida
entry.summary: Thomas Wayne Markle, the father of Meghan Markle, was arrested Friday in Florida on a federal charge of possessing child pornography after investigators said they found suspected child sexual abuse material in two Los Angeles-area storage units he had rented for nearly two decades. Thomas Markle, 82, of Lakeland, is charged with one count of possession of child pornography, according to federal prosecutors. He was expected to make his initial appearance Friday in federal court in Tampa. The FBI investigation began after authorities learned in October that a person had signed an affidavit describing the discovery of suspected child sexual abuse material among Markle's belongings in the Philippines, according to an affidavit filed with the criminal complaint. Investigators later learned Thomas Markle rented a storage unit in the Los Angeles area. Information provided by the person who reported the material in the Philippines eventually led authorities to a second storage unit, the affidavit states. Federal agents obtained search warrants for both units, which investigators said Thomas Markle had rented since 2008. According to prosecutors, his most recent payments for the units were made through automatic payments last month. During searches of the units, FBI agents seized roughly 78 items, including slides, film negatives and books containing suspected child sexual abuse material, according to the news release. Federal authorities allege some of the photographs show an adult man, identified by a witness as Thomas Markle, with prepubescent girls. Investigators said other photographs appeared to depict Markle with children in various stages of undress. 'These allegations are extremely serious, and we will prosecute Mr. Markle to the fullest extent of federal law,' First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli said. FBI officials said the case demonstrates the importance of reporting suspected child exploitation to law enforcement. 'This case highlights the importance of the involvement of the public, even if its a family member or close friend, to be vigilant and speak up if they have information on individuals they suspect may be preying on and exploiting our children,' Patrick Grandy, assistant director in charge of the FBIs Los Angeles Field Office, said. Thomas Markle is the estranged father of Meghan Markle, the Duchess of Sussex and wife of Prince Harry. The FBI is investigating the case. If convicted, Thomas Markle faces a statutory maximum sentence of 20

If convicted, Thomas Markle faces a statutory maximum sentence of 20 years in federal prison.His arrest follows reports by The Sun, a British tabloid newspaper, that Meghan's half-brother found a collection of child sexual abuse images while clearing out the home of their father in the Philippines.Meghan recently said she was "deeply distressed" by allegations that a collection of child sexual abuse images had been found at her father’s former home. She also revealed that a letter containing “troubling allegations” about him had been sent to London police in 2018."It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated,” Meghan said of the letter. "I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children was for one reason: to protect them.”Meghan, an American citizen who starred in the U.S. television drama “Suits,” married Harry at Windsor Castle in 2018. They have two children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet.Her father, a retired television lighting and photography director, did not attend the wedding, prompting extensive coverage in the British media of Meghan's estrangement from her father.Thomas Markle Sr. was living in the Philippines earlier this year when he suffered a stroke and had his left leg amputated. That forced him to return to the U.S.The Sun reported that Thomas Markle Jr. recently found “hundreds, if not thousands” of child sex abuse images in boxes at his father’s former home in Cebu City, in the Philippines, when he was clearing out the property.Markle Jr. told the newspaper that he reported the images to police in the Philippines and contacted the FBI."I have supported, cared for him and helped him for years — but that stops now," Markle Jr. "I won't speak to my father ever again unless I’m called to give evidence against him."

entry.title: Martin County flooding leaves cattle farmers struggling, residents demanding solutions - WPBF
entry.summary: Martin County flooding leaves cattle farmers struggling, residents demanding solutions    WPBF
entry.article_text: Floodwaters continue to inundate properties in Martin County, leaving cattle farmers struggling to care for their animals and residents concerned about how much longer the water will remain. Residents in the Trailside community say water from neighboring properties is flowing into their drainage system, causing widespread flooding. Flooding threatens cattle, farm operations Hungryland Farms normally operates a 20-acre rotational grazing system for its Florida Cracker cattle. The owner, Melissa, said much of the pasture is now underwater, forcing the animals onto the farm’s elevated driveway. "We're starting to lose big sections of the driveway. We have them concentrated up the house pad, but if we lose too much more, we're just going to have to figure out a way to evacuate them somewhere," she said. Some cattle have struggled to navigate the water, and Melissa said the farm is concerned about losing access to its property as flooding continues. For now, the farm is bringing in hay and hay cubes to keep the cattle on their regular diet while monitoring potential health risks from floodwaters. "We’re more just concerned with the health and safety of our cattle," Melissa said. Melissa said the farm has an emergency contact with the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Natural Resources Conservation Service if the animals face imminent danger. "We don’t know how long we’re going to be here," she said. HOA says solution is unclear Kyla Shay, president of the Trailside Homeowners Association, said the community’s drainage system is designed to handle water from its 41 lots and designated neighboring properties. However, Shay said water from outside that system is now flowing through county-owned land and other neighboring properties before reaching the community’s southern canal. We can’t handle theirs," Shay said. The flooding has also affected neighboring pastures and reached areas near Bridge Road and an electrical substation, according to Shay. She said some electrical transformers are partially underwater, septic systems are overwhelmed and residents have been warned their well water could be compromised. "The health department issued warnings this morning to me that our water wells could be compromised because of bacteria, because of the standing water," Shay said. Since their septic systems are submerged, Shay said homeowners have been unable to shower or do laundry. County says repairs must wait WPBF 25 News reached out to Martin County about their concerns and learned the county recently acquired approximately 315 acres of land in the area, known as the Elise J. A county spokesperson said establishing access has been their immediate priority so staff can assess conditions and respond. The county said it is working with the Hobe-St. Lucie Conservancy District to address a breach affecting drainage into its irrigation canal and that the agencies jointly determined repairs should wait until water levels recede. The county said current conditions make hauling and placing sand unsafe and potentially damaging to the levee. Material could also wash into the canal before crews establish a stable repair. "County staff will continue to monitor water levels and site conditions in close coordination with the Hobe-St. Lucie Conservancy District," a county spokesperson said. The county said it will move forward with repairs when conditions allow safe work without compromising the levee. It is also evaluating longer-term options to improve outflow and reduce the risk of flooding happening again. Residents want a long-term solution Shay said the homeowners association has been working with water engineers and other experts to understand how long the flooding could last. "It's probably going to be late January, February before we can see a break, and that's assuming that the south canal wall does not collapse and immediately dump all the water on us," she said. Melissa said the farm’s drainage system normally provides room for water to collect during the rainy season, but the amount coming from outside the property has overwhelmed it. "We have a very extensive drainage system, but it’s just not equipped to handle this amount of water," Melissa said. Both women said they want neighboring properties and the agencies responsible for drainage to address the problem. For now, Martin County said it will continue monitoring conditions and coordinating with the conservancy district before attempting repairs. Meanwhile, Melissa said the farm is focused on keeping its cattle safe as water continues to surround the property.

entry.title: St. Lucie County asks residents, businesses to report flood damage through online survey
entry.summary: St. Lucie County is asking residents, businesses and agricultural property owners affected by recent flooding to report damage through an online survey as officials work to document the extent of the impacts. The survey is open to property owners and tenants across the county, including Fort Pierce, Port St. Lucie, St. Lucie Village and unincorporated St. Lucie County. WATCH: Heavy rains flood Port St. Lucie roads earlier this week Heavy rain floods Port St. Lucie roads, leaving drivers stranded County officials said the information collected will be shared with local, state and federal partners to help assess the extent of the flooding and guide recovery efforts. The survey asks respondents to provide the property's location and building type, along with basic information about flooding and damage. It also includes questions about private wells used for household water and septic systems. People can complete the flood impact survey here through Friday, Nov. 20. County officials stressed that completing the survey is not an application for assistance and does not guarantee that funding will be available. Instead, the information will be used to help officials better understand the scope of the damage. Anyone with multiple affected structures should submit a separate survey for each one. The county is seeking reports about impacts to buildings and their associated systems rather than flooding limited to yards or surrounding property. Residents should only report conditions they have already observed. Officials are warning people not to enter unsafe buildings, walk through floodwater or touch electrical equipment in order to assess damage. Anyone who needs help completing the survey can contact the St. Lucie County Community Services Department at 772-462-1777 or comm_info@stlucieco.gov.

entry.title: Strong El Niño could bring wetter winter, increased flood and severe weather risk to South Florida
entry.summary: With a very strong El Nio event in the Pacific, the U.S. weather pattern is significantly impacted, especially in winter. Historically, El Nio brings stormier weather for the southern United States, including Florida. According to the National Weather Service (NWS) Miami, above-normal rainfall is anticipated for our dry season with a higher risk for flood events and severe weather including tornadoes. This happens as El Nio drives the subtropical jet stream farther south across the U.S. during the winter and dry season and generally steers more storm systems eastward. The NWS says due to the strength of the El Nio, which could match or exceed the historic 19971998 event as the strongest recorded (since 1950), confidence is high for a higher risk of strong storms. The 1997-1998 El Nio is tied to multiple severe weather events and the deadliest tornado outbreak in Florida back in February of '98. AFFECT ON WINTER TEMPERATURES Although more storm systems are in the forecast, it doesn't mean we will necessarily see more cold snaps or days with freezing temperatures. Because the dominant subtropical jet stream drives more southern storm systems, cold air masses from the north rarely penetrate into Florida. This lowers, but does not completely eliminate the overall likelihood of extreme cold events. The NWS forecasts near-average temperatures for South Florida as more frequent storm systems tends to depress daily high temperatures, while streams of milder Pacific air keep overnight lows higher than normal. IMPACT ON DROUGHT AND WILDFIRES Due to these moist conditions, significant wildfire activity is projected to remain below normal through the winter and potentially extending into the spring.

entry.title: Who will lead Congress? Leadership battles take center stage after midterms
entry.summary: With Democrats poised to take control of both chambers of Congress, attention is quickly turning from the 2026 midterm elections to the leadership battles that will determine who guides the new House and Senate majorities. Leadership elections are expected to begin next week, with Democrats facing some internal pressure over their current leaders and House Republicans preparing for a potentially tight contest of their own. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer and House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries are expected to remain at the top of their respective caucuses. Jeffries would be in position to become House speaker, while Schumer would become Senate majority leader. Both, however, have faced calls from some progressive activists and incoming lawmakers for a change in leadership. Critics argue Democratic leaders did not push back aggressively enough against President Donald Trump while the party was in the minority. Jackson said he plans to push Democratic leaders on priorities including Medicare for All. entry.title: Catholic Charities responds to Palm Beach County crises while opening People of Hope Museum
entry.summary: Catholic Charities of the Diocese of Palm Beach is balancing four community efforts this week, from responding to people displaced by a plane crash and flooding to opening an interactive museum designed to help people better understand poverty. Ellen T. entry.title: Thomas Markle, father of Meghan Markle, arrested on charges related to child sexual abuse material in Florida
entry.summary: Thomas Wayne Markle, the father of Meghan Markle, was arrested Friday morning at an assisted living facility in Lakeland, Florida, on a federal charge of possessing child pornography after investigators said they found suspected child sexual abuse material in two Los Angeles-area storage units he had rented for nearly two decades. The 82-year-old Lakeland resident is charged with one count of possession of child pornography, according to federal prosecutors. He was expected to make his initial appearance Friday in federal court in Tampa. The FBI investigation began after authorities learned in October that a person had signed an affidavit describing the discovery of suspected child sexual abuse material among Thomas Markle's belongings in the Philippines, according to an affidavit filed with the criminal complaint. Investigators later learned Thomas Markle rented a storage unit in the Los Angeles area. Information provided by the person who reported the material in the Philippines eventually led authorities to a second storage unit, according to the affidavit. Federal agents obtained search warrants for both units, which investigators said Thomas Markle had rented since 2008. According to prosecutors, his most recent payments for the units were made through automatic payments last month. During searches of the units, FBI agents seized roughly 78 items, including slides, film negatives and books containing suspected child sexual abuse material, according to the news release. Federal authorities allege some of the photographs show an adult man, identified by a witness as Thomas Markle, with prepubescent girls. Investigators said other photographs appeared to depict Markle with children in various stages of undress.
